versions.english: The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein

sources.versionTitle: The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein

pairs.english: In the beginning of the creation by G-d [Elokim, the attribute of justice,]

of the heavens and the earth, [G-d first intending to create the world with the attribute of justice but then granting precedence to the attribute of mercy (Yod-Key-Vav-Key), seeing that the world could not otherwise endure],
the earth was vacuous and void,
and there was darkness upon the face of the deep [i.e., the waters],
and the "wind of G-d" [the Throne of Glory, impelled by His utterance] hovered over the face of the waters.
And G-d said: Let there be light!
And there was light.
And G-d saw that the light was good, [and that it was not appropriate for light and darkness to serve in combination]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
pairs.english: and G-d separated between the light and the darkness, [making the day the domain of the first and the night the domain of the second].
And G-d called the light day,
and the darkness He called night.
And it was evening and it was morning, the day of the One, [the angels not being created until the second day].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let there be a firmament [i.e., let the firmament be hardened] in the midst of the waters, [the upper waters being at a distance from the firmament just as the lower waters are],
and let it divide between waters and waters.
And G-d made [i.e., fixed in place] the firmament,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ
pairs.english: and He divided between the waters below the firmament and the waters above the firmament;
and it was so.
And G-d called the firmament shamayim [sa mayim - it "carries" water (the upper waters); sham mayim - water is there; esh umayim - fire and water (the firmament being a combination of the two)].
And it was evening, and it was morning, the second day.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let the waters below the heavens, [which were spread over the entire earth], be gathered into one place [the ocean],
and let the dry land be seen;
and it was so.
And G-d called the dry land "earth,"
and the gathering of the waters He called "seas" [(plural, fish from different regions of the sea having distinctive tastes)],
and G-d saw that it was good, [the "work of the waters" being completed on that day].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תַּֽדְשֵׁ֤א הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ דֶּ֗שֶׁא עֵ֚שֶׂב מַזְרִ֣יעַ זֶ֔רַע
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let the earth put forth [a blanket of] herbage, grass yielding seed,

pairs.hebrew: עֵ֣ץ פְּרִ֞י עֹ֤שֶׂה פְּרִי֙ לְמִינ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: fruit-tree, [the tree tasting like the fruit], giving fruit of its kind, whose seed is in it [to grow a tree of the same kind] upon the earth;
and it was so.

pairs.hebrew: וַתּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ דֶּ֠שֶׁא עֵ֣שֶׂב מַזְרִ֤יעַ זֶ֙רַע֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ
pairs.english: And the earth put forth herbage, grass yielding seed according to its kind [though not having been commanded to do so],
and tree giving fruit [(but not "fruit-tree" as commanded (11), for which the earth was subsequently punished, together with Adam)], whose seed is in it according to its kind.
And G-d saw that it was good.
And it was evening, and it was morning,
the third day.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let there be [suspended] luminaries in the firmament of the heaven [(The luminaries, like all things pertaining to heaven and to earth, had been created on the first day, but each of the particular creations was activated on its particular day.)]
to divide between the day and the night, [after the first light had been secreted for the righteous for the world to come.]

And let them serve for signs [(eclipses being omens of ill)], and for festivals, [reckoned by the New Moon], and for days, [the sun and the moon serving for half a day respectively], and for years, [completing their course through the zodiac in 365 days].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֤וּ לִמְאוֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And let them [in addition] be luminaries in the firmament of the heaven to illuminate the earth;
and it was so.
And G-d made the two great luminaries [(They were created of equal size, but when the moon protested "two kings reigning with one crown," it was diminished)],
the great luminary for governance of the day,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הַמָּא֤וֹר הַקָּטֹן֙ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְאֵ֖ת הַכּוֹכָבִֽים׃
pairs.english: and the small luminary for governance of the night, and the stars, [(G-d multiplying the moon's hosts to "appease" it for its diminution)].
And G-d set them in the firmament of the heaven
to give light upon the earth.
And to rule by day and by night,
and to divide between the light and the darkness.
And G-d saw that it was good.
And it was evening, and it was morning,
the fourth day.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let the waters swarm a swarming (sheretz) [creatures not higher than the ground (e.g., flies, worms, rodents, fish)] infused with life,

pairs.hebrew: וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and birds flying above the earth on the face of the firmament of heaven.
And G-d created the leviathans

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֣ת כׇּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּ֣ה ׀ הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם
pairs.english: and all the creeping life-infused creatures, swarmed by the waters according to their kinds,
and every winged bird according to its kind,
and G-d saw that it was good.
And G-d blessed them, saying:
Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas,
and let the birds multiply in the earth.
And it was evening, and it was morning,
the fifth day.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ נֶ֤פֶשׁ חַיָּה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let the earth bring forth [(it already having been created on the first day)] (every) life-infused creature according to its kind:
beast, creeping thing, and animal of the earth according to its kind;
and it was so. [It was fully formed.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֩ אֶת־חַיַּ֨ת הָאָ֜רֶץ לְמִינָ֗הּ וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ
pairs.english: And G-d made [fully formed] (every) animal of the earth according to its kind and (every) beast according to its kind,
and creeping thing according to its kind;
and G-d saw that it was good.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ
pairs.english: And G-d said: Let us make man [(G-d in His humility "asking leave" of the angels)] in our image according to our likeness [to understand and to know],
and yirdu [connoting "they shall have dominion over" (if they are virtuous) or (if they are not), "they shall be humbled before"] the fish of the sea, the birds of the heaven,
the beasts, and all the earth, and all the creeping things that creep on the earth.
And G-d created the man in his mould [that He had cast for him (Adam, as opposed to the other creations, being created by "hand" and not by pronouncement)];
in the image of G-d He created him;
male and female He created them [on the sixth day, forming Eve from Adam's side].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָם֮ אֱלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים
pairs.english: And G-d blessed them, and G-d said to them:

Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it [(also readable as "subdue her," connoting both that the mitzvah of procreation is his and not hers, and that he is to keep her from being "free" with herself)],

pairs.hebrew: וּרְד֞וּ בִּדְגַ֤ת הַיָּם֙ וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּבְכׇל־חַיָּ֖ה הָֽרֹמֶ֥שֶׂת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and have dominion over the fish of the sea and the birds of the heaven, and over all the animals that range the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־כׇּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב ׀ זֹרֵ֣עַ זֶ֗רַע אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כׇל־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: And G-d said: Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the face of the earth
and every tree which has in it fruit of a tree, bearing seed.
To you shall it be for food, [man not being permitted to kill animals for food until after the flood].

pairs.hebrew: וּֽלְכׇל־חַיַּ֣ת הָ֠אָ֠רֶץ וּלְכׇל־ע֨וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וּלְכֹ֣ל ׀ רוֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה
pairs.english: And to all the animals of the earth and to all the birds of heaven, and to all that creeps upon the earth, which has a living soul,
(I have given) every green herb for food.
And it was so.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־ט֖וֹב מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: And G-d saw all that He had made, and, behold, it was very good;
and it was evening and it was morning the [hah] sixth day, [(signaling acceptance of the five (heh) books of the Law as a sine qua non for the creation)].
And the heavens and the earth were finished,
and all of their hosts.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה
pairs.english: And G-d completed on [i.e., precisely upon the advent of] the seventh day His work that He had done,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכׇּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
pairs.english: and He rested on the seventh day, from all the work that He had done.
And G-d blessed the seventh day [through the manna (a presage of the future), double the normal amount being provided on the sixth day],
and He sanctified it, [through the manna, none falling on the Sabbath],

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכׇּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃ {פ}
pairs.english: for on it He rested from all of His work which the L-rd had created to do. [i.e., What was to have been done on the Sabbath was done on the sixth day, the work of that day being doubled.]
These [the above-mentioned] are the engenderings of the heaven and the earth, when they were created,

pairs.hebrew: בְּי֗וֹם עֲשׂ֛וֹת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: on the day the L-rd G-d made earth and heaven [(whence it is derived that they were all created on the first day (see 1:14)].

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹ֣ל ׀ שִׂ֣יחַ הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה טֶ֚רֶם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ וְכׇל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה טֶ֣רֶם יִצְמָ֑ח
pairs.english: And every plant of the field was not yet in the earth, and every grass of the field had not yet sprouted [above the ground (the third-day sprouting (12) remaining beneath the surface)],

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הִמְטִ֜יר יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: for the L-rd G-d [(the first, Yod-Key-Vav-Key, being His name; the second, Elokim, connoting Ruler and Judge)] had not yet caused it to rain upon the earth,
for there was no man to work the ground [and to appreciate the rain, until Adam was created, who recognized that rain was needed for the world, prayed for it, and "secured" it].
And [for the creation of man (1:27)] a vapor rose from the earth
and watered the entire face of the ground, [water, as it were, being added to the "dough" for the "kneading" of man].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֩יצֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֗ם עָפָר֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d formed (vayitzer) [two yods for two "formings," one for this world, one for the resurrection (as opposed to the creation of the beasts (19), where only one yod is written)] the man, dust from the [four corners of the] earth.
And He blew into his nostrils a soul of life,
and man became a vital soul, [having speech and understanding (as opposed to the beasts)].
And the L-rd G-d planted a garden in Eden from the east,
and He placed there the man that He had formed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּצְמַ֞ח יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כׇּל־עֵ֛ץ נֶחְמָ֥ד לְמַרְאֶ֖ה וְט֣וֹב לְמַאֲכָ֑ל
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d caused to sprout from the ground [in the garden of Eden] every tree desirable to the sight and good for eating,
and the tree of life in the very midst of the garden,
and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
And a river goes out of Eden to water the garden;
and from there it parts and becomes four heads.
The name of the first, Pishon ["the bountiful" (the Nile)].

pairs.hebrew: ה֣וּא הַסֹּבֵ֗ב אֵ֚ת כׇּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחֲוִילָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃
pairs.english: It is that which goes round the entire land of Chavilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is good.
There is the bedollach and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river, Gichon ["roaring"].
It is that which goes round the entire land of Kush.
And the name of the third river, Chidekel [so called because its waters are pungent (chad) and light (kal)].
It is that which goes east of Ashur.
And the fourth river, Perath ["waxing" (the most distinctive of all, being mentioned in conjunction with Eretz Yisrael (see Deuteronomy 1:7)].
And the L-rd G-d "took" the man [with pleasant, enticing words],
and He placed him in the garden of Eden to work it and to guard it.
And the L-rd G-d commanded the man, saying:
Of every tree of the garden you may eat.

pairs.hebrew: וּמֵעֵ֗ץ הַדַּ֙עַת֙ ט֣וֹב וָרָ֔ע לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם אֲכׇלְךָ֥ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃
pairs.english: For on the day that you eat of it you shall die.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹא־ט֛וֹב הֱי֥וֹת הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְבַדּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d said: It is not good that the man be alone [and "one" (i.e., unique in having no mate) among the terrestrial creatures, as the L-rd is One among the celestial creatures — two deities, as it were];
I shall make him a help [(If he merits it, she is a help)], against him [(If he does not merit it, she is against him, contending with him)]. [(see 2:20)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֩צֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה כׇּל־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d formed from the earth all of the animals of the field [(same as 1:25)] and [also] all of the birds of the heavens, [forming them from slime (a combination of water (1:20) and earth)],
and He brought (them) [on the very same day] to the man to see what he would call them.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקְרָא־ל֧וֹ הָֽאָדָ֛ם נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה ה֥וּא שְׁמֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And every living creature that the man named — that is its name [forever].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם שֵׁמ֗וֹת לְכׇל־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּלְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And the man named every beast and bird of heaven and all the animals of the field [and saw that each had its mate],
but for the man he did not find a help against him. [(see 2:18)]
And the L-rd G-d cast a deep sleep upon the man and he slept.
And He took one of his sides
and He closed it up [the incision site] with flesh beneath it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֩בֶן֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים ׀ אֶֽת־הַצֵּלָ֛ע אֲשֶׁר־לָקַ֥ח מִן־הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְאִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d fashioned the side that He had taken from the man into a woman, ["building" her broad beneath and narrow above (like a wheat bin) so that the fetus not weigh down too heavily upon her sides],
and He brought her to the man.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֘אמֶר֮ הָֽאָדָם֒ זֹ֣את הַפַּ֗עַם עֶ֚צֶם מֵֽעֲצָמַ֔י וּבָשָׂ֖ר מִבְּשָׂרִ֑י
pairs.english: And the man said: This time [(Adam having lived with every beast and not having found gratification)], bone of my bone and flesh of my flesh.
This shall be called ishah (woman),
for from ish (man) was this taken [(whence it is derived that the world was created with the holy tongue)].
Therefore, [(the Divine Spirit speaking, interdicting illicit relations to the Noachides)], a man shall leave his father and his mother
and cleave to his wife,
and they shall become one flesh [in their child, who is formed from both].
And both of them were naked, the man and his wife,
and they were not ashamed, [for they did not know the way of modesty, to distinguish between good and evil, until they had eaten of the tree of knowledge (of good and evil)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the serpent was more subtle than all the animals of the field that the L-rd G-d had made,
and [seeing them naked and copulating openly, and desiring her,] he said to the woman: Can it be that G-d has said:
You shall not eat of all the trees of the garden? [speaking thus though seeing them eating from all the other trees, in order to turn the subject to that tree].
And the woman said to the serpent:
Of the fruit of the trees of the garden, we may eat.

pairs.hebrew: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים
pairs.english: And from the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, G-d said:

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן־תְּמֻתֽוּן׃
pairs.english: You shall not eat of it and you shall not touch it, [(Eve "sealing her 'destruction' by her 'addition'")] lest you die.
And the serpent said to the woman:
you shall not die. [He pushed her until she touched the tree and said to her: Just as there is no death in touching it, there is no death in eating from it.]

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכׇלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: For G-d knows that on the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened

and you will be like G-d [creators of worlds], knowing good and evil. [i.e., G-d ate of it and created the world, and you, likewise, will be creators of worlds by eating of it. Knowing this, and desiring "exclusivity," He forbids it to you.]

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל
pairs.english: And the woman saw [i.e., she espoused the words of the serpent] that the tree was good for eating, [making one like G-d],

pairs.hebrew: וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה־ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל
pairs.english: and that it was desirable for the eyes, [viz.: "your eyes will be opened"], and that the tree was auspicious for knowing [viz.: "knowing good and evil"],
and she took of its fruit and she ate,
and she gave also to her husband with her [so that she not die and he live and marry another], and he ate.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּפָּקַ֙חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם
pairs.english: And the eyes of both were opened and they knew that they were naked [bereft of their one mitzvah],

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃
pairs.english: and they put together fig leaves and made themselves girdles. [(The tree of knowledge was a fig tree. "Wherein they offended, they were amended.")]

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ק֨וֹל יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם
pairs.english: And they heard the voice of the L-rd G-d sounding in the garden in the direction of (the descent of) the sun, [i.e., the west],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃
pairs.english: and the man and his wife hid before the L-rd G-d in the midst of the trees of the garden.
And the L-rd G-d called to the man,
and He said to him: "Where are You?" [this, in order to give him time to collect himself]
And he said: I heard Your voice in the garden
and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה
pairs.english: And He said: Who told you that you were naked? [i.e., Where did you learn to be ashamed of your nakedness?]

pairs.hebrew: הֲמִן־הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכׇל־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃
pairs.english: Did you eat of the tree from which I bade you not to eat?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י
pairs.english: And the man said: The woman that You gave with me, [(Adam here denies G-d's boon)] —
she gave me of the tree and I ate.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d said to the woman: What is this that you have done?
And the woman said: The serpent deceived me and I ate.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֶֽל־הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d said to the serpent: Because you did this,

pairs.hebrew: אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכׇּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: you are more accursed than all the beasts and all the animals of the field.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כׇּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: On your belly shall you go, and dust shall you eat all the days of your life.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵיבָ֣ה ׀ אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And hatred shall I place between you and between the woman, [whom you seduced with your wiles] and between your seed and her seed.
He will crush your head
and you will hiss at his heel [to bite him].

pairs.hebrew: אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הַרְבָּ֤ה אַרְבֶּה֙ עִצְּבוֹנֵ֣ךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵ֔ךְ
pairs.english: To the woman He said: I shall increase your distress [in rearing children] and your [pain in] pregnancy.
In travail shall you bear children,
and to your husband shall be your desire [for cohabitation, in spite of which you will not have the boldness to solicit him verbally], and he shall "rule" over you [in this regard].

pairs.hebrew: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֘עְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּ֒ךָ֒ וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ מִן־הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: And to the man he said: Because you heeded your wife's voice and ate of the tree whereof I commanded you not to eat,
cursed is the earth [(whence you were begotten)] for you. [(It shall spawn "accursed" things for you, like flies, fleas and ants)].
In toil shall you eat of it all the days of your life.
And thorns and thistles [artichokes and cardoon (which can be eaten only with special preparation)] will it sprout for you [when you sow it],
and you will eat the herbs of the field.
With the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread

pairs.hebrew: עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ
pairs.english: until you return to the ground. For from it were you taken.
For dust you are and to dust you will return.
And [(reversion to 2:20, "And the man named every beast, etc.")] the man called his wife Chavah ["vivifying"],
for she was the mother of all the living.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֩עַשׂ֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְאָדָ֧ם וּלְאִשְׁתּ֛וֹ כׇּתְנ֥וֹת ע֖וֹר
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d made for the man and his wife skin-vestments
and He clothed them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע
pairs.english: And the L-rd G-d said: Behold, man has become like one of us [(He is unique among the terrestrial creations as I am unique among the celestial. And what is his uniqueness?)] knowing good and evil [(such knowledge not obtaining with beasts and animals)].

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ פֶּן־יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם׃
pairs.english: And now, perhaps he will put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life and eat and live forever [and draw the other creatures after him to regard him as a deity].
And the Lord God sent him from the garden of Eden
to work the ground whence he was taken.
And He drove out the man,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן־עֵ֜דֶן אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֙רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת
pairs.english: and He set east of the garden of Eden the cherubs [angels of destruction] and the flash of the revolving sword [(to intimidate him against re-entering)]
to guard the path of the tree of life.
And the man had known Chavah his wife
and she had conceived and had borne [(even before the episode of the tree of knowledge)], [a twin girl] with Cain.
And she said: "I have acquired [(kanithi, like "Cain")] a man with the L-rd" [(my husband and I being "partners" with Him in the creation of Cain)].
And she bore again [(a twin sister)] with his brother, with [(i.e., another twin sister, with)] Abel.
And Abel was a shepherd,
and Cain was a tiller of the soil.
And it was, after some time,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: that Cain brought of the fruits [(of the poorest of them)] of the ground, a gift to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן
pairs.english: And Abel brought — he, too — of the first-born of his flock and of their fats.
And the L-rd turned to Abel and to his gift. [Fire descended (from heaven) and consumed his offering.]
And to Cain and to his gift He did not turn.
And Cain was sorely wroth, and his face fell.
And the L-rd said to Cain:

pairs.hebrew: לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: Why are you wroth, and why is your face fallen?
If you make amends, will you not be forgiven?

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תֵיטִ֔יב לַפֶּ֖תַח חַטָּ֣את רֹבֵ֑ץ
pairs.english: And if you do not make amends, at the opening [of your grave] your sin lies [i.e., is preserved],
and to you is its [the evil inclination's] desire [to lead you astray]; but you can rule over it.
And Cain spoke to Abel, [contentiously, seeking a pretext to kill him],
and it was, when they were in the field,
that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־קַ֔יִן אֵ֖י הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Cain [(gently, by way of "preparing" him)]: "Where is Abel your brother?"

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי הֲשֹׁמֵ֥ר אָחִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃
pairs.english: And he said [(negating Divine omniscience)]: "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
And He said: What have you done?

pairs.hebrew: ק֚וֹל דְּמֵ֣י אָחִ֔יךָ צֹעֲקִ֥ים אֵלַ֖י מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
pairs.english: The voice of your brother's bloods [his blood and that of his unborn children] are crying out to Me from the ground.
And, now, you shall be cursed more than the earth [has already been cursed for its sin (see 1:12). And in this, too, it has continued to sin —]

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּצְתָ֣ה אֶת־פִּ֔יהָ לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־דְּמֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: in that it has opened its mouth to take your brother's bloods from your hand.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י תַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹֽא־תֹסֵ֥ף תֵּת־כֹּחָ֖הּ לָ֑ךְ
pairs.english: [(the additional curse:)] When you till the soil, it shall no longer give her strength to you.
A vagabond and a wanderer shall you be in the land, [not being permitted to live in one place].
And Cain said to the L-rd:
"Is my sin too great [for You, the 'bearer' of heaven and earth] to bear?"

pairs.hebrew: הֵן֩ גֵּרַ֨שְׁתָּ אֹתִ֜י הַיּ֗וֹם מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וּמִפָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶסָּתֵ֑ר
pairs.english: Behold, You have driven me this day from the face of the ground, and from Your face shall I be hid,
and I shall be a vagabond and a wanderer in the earth,
and whoever finds me will kill me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהֹוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כׇּל־הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to him: Therefore, whoever kills Cain … At the end of seven [generations] it shall be avenged (see 24).

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהֹוָ֤ה לְקַ֙יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־אֹת֖וֹ כׇּל־מֹצְאֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And the L-rd made for Cain a sign that he not be smitten by any who find him.
And Cain went forth from before the L-rd [in assumed humility]

and he dwelt in the land of Nod [whither all the exiles betake themselves ("nadim")] east of Eden [where his father was exiled (3:24) and where (in the east) the cities of refuge are located (Deuteronomy 4:41)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֙יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־חֲנ֑וֹךְ
pairs.english: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and she bore Chanoch.
And he built a city,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃
pairs.english: and he called the name of the city after the name of his son Chanoch [as a memorial to him].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Irad was born to Chanoch, and Irad begot Mechuyael,

pairs.hebrew: וּמְחִיָּיאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־לָֽמֶךְ׃
pairs.english: and Mechiyael begot Methushael, and Methushael begot Lamech.
And Lamech took for himself two wives [(all of this being mentioned as bearing out "at the end of seven generations" (15)],

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃
pairs.english: the name of the first, Adah, and the name of the second, Tzilah.
And Adah bore Yaval.

pairs.hebrew: ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃
pairs.english: He was the father of those who dwell in tents raising cattle, [moving from place to place for fresh pasture].
And the name of his brother was Yuval.

pairs.hebrew: ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כׇּל־תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃
pairs.english: He was the father of all who play harp and pipe.
And Tzilah — she, too, bore Tuval-Cain [lit., "refiner of Cain" (i.e., of his trade — murder)],
forging all tools of copper and iron.
And the sister of Tuval-Cain was Na'amah.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לֶ֜מֶךְ לְנָשָׁ֗יו עָדָ֤ה וְצִלָּה֙ שְׁמַ֣עַן קוֹלִ֔י נְשֵׁ֣י לֶ֔מֶךְ הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִ֑י
pairs.english: And Lemech said to his wives, Adah and Tzilah, [who had separated from him after he had (unwittingly) killed Cain and Tuval-Cain:] Hear my voice, wives of Lemech. Heed my speech.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ הָרַ֙גְתִּי֙ לְפִצְעִ֔י וְיֶ֖לֶד לְחַבֻּרָתִֽי׃
pairs.english: Did I kill a man [Cain] by my [wilfully inflicted] wound, and a child [Tuval-Cain] by my blow?
If Cain, [who killed wilfully,] were avenged [only after] seven generations,
should Lemech, [who killed unwittingly, not be granted] seventy and seven!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨דַע אָדָ֥ם עוֹד֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן
pairs.english: And Adam knew his wife again [after having reproached Lemech's wives for separating from their husbands, and having himself been reproached for separating from Eve after death was decreed for mankind], and she bore a son,
and she called his name Sheth;

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י שָֽׁת־לִ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ זֶ֣רַע אַחֵ֔ר תַּ֣חַת הֶ֔בֶל כִּ֥י הֲרָג֖וֹ קָֽיִן׃
pairs.english: for (she said) G-d set (shath) for me other seed in place of Abel whom Cain killed.

pairs.hebrew: וּלְשֵׁ֤ת גַּם־הוּא֙ יֻלַּד־בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱנ֑וֹשׁ
pairs.english: And unto Sheth, too, was born a son, and he called his name Enosh.
Then [men and images] were called profanely in the name of the L-rd, [being rendered deities].
This is the numeration of the generations of Adam
on the day G-d created man [(Adam begetting on the day he was born)].
In the likeness of G-d He made him.
Male and female He created them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָ֗ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמָם֙ אָדָ֔ם בְּי֖וֹם הִבָּֽרְאָֽם׃
pairs.english: And He blessed them, and He called their name Adam on the day He created them.
And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years [after having separated from Eve],
and he (then) begot (a son) in his likeness according to his image,
and he called his name Sheth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ יְמֵי־אָדָ֗ם אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־שֵׁ֔ת שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵאֹ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the days of Adam after he begot Sheth were eight hundred years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְי֞וּ כׇּל־יְמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁר־חַ֔י תְּשַׁ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Adam, which he lived, were nine hundred and thirty years,
and he died.
And Sheth lived a hundred and five years
and he begot Enosh.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־שֵׁ֗ת אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־אֱנ֔וֹשׁ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Sheth lived, after he begot Enosh, eight hundred and seven years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵי־שֵׁ֔ת שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Sheth were nine hundred and twelve years,
and he died.
And Enosh lived ninety years
and he begot Keinan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י אֱנ֗וֹשׁ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־קֵינָ֔ן חֲמֵ֤שׁ עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Enosh lived, after he begot Keinan, eight hundred and fifteen years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵ֣י אֱנ֔וֹשׁ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years,
and he died.
And Keinan lived seventy years
and he begot Mahalalel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י קֵינָ֗ן אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־מַֽהֲלַלְאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Keinan lived, after he begot Mahalalel, eight hundred and forty years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵ֣י קֵינָ֔ן עֶ֣שֶׂר שָׁנִ֔ים וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Keinan were nine hundred and ten years,
and he died.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י מַֽהֲלַלְאֵ֔ל חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים וְשִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Mahalalel lived sixty-five years
and he begot Yared.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י מַֽהֲלַלְאֵ֗ל אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־יֶ֔רֶד שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Mahalalel lived, after he begot Yared, eight hundred and thirty years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵ֣י מַהֲלַלְאֵ֔ל חָמֵ֤שׁ וְתִשְׁעִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years,
and he died.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־יֶ֕רֶד שְׁתַּ֧יִם וְשִׁשִּׁ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּמְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Yered lived a hundred and sixty-two years
and he begot Chanoch.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־יֶ֗רֶד אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־חֲנ֔וֹךְ שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Yered lived, after he begot Chanoch, eight hundred years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵי־יֶ֔רֶד שְׁתַּ֤יִם וְשִׁשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Yered were nine hundred and sixty-two years,
and he died.
And Chanoch lived sixty-five years
and he begot Methuselah.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְהַלֵּ֨ךְ חֲנ֜וֹךְ אֶת־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־מְתוּשֶׁ֔לַח שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Chanoch walked with G-d after he begot Methuselah three hundred years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Chanoch

pairs.hebrew: חָמֵ֤שׁ וְשִׁשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: were three hundred and sixty-five years.
And Chanoch walked with G-d,
and he was not, for G-d took him [before his time, so that he not depart from his righteousness.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י מְתוּשֶׁ֔לַח שֶׁ֧בַע וּשְׁמֹנִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּמְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Methuselah lived a hundred and eighty-seven years
and he begot Lamech.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י מְתוּשֶׁ֗לַח אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־לֶ֔מֶךְ שְׁתַּ֤יִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Methuselah lived, after he begot Lemech, seven hundred and eighty-two years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְיוּ֙ כׇּל־יְמֵ֣י מְתוּשֶׁ֔לַח תֵּ֤שַׁע וְשִׁשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years,
and he died.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־לֶ֕מֶךְ שְׁתַּ֧יִם וּשְׁמֹנִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּמְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Lemech lived a hundred and eighty-two years
and he begot a son [ben, from whom the world was built (nivneh)].
And he called his name Noach, saying:
This one will "ease us" (yenachamenu) of our deeds and of the toil of our hands
from the earth, which the L-rd cursed, [(Noach providing plowing tools for them, and the earth ceasing to sprout thorns and thistles whenever they sowed wheat)].

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־לֶ֗מֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־נֹ֔חַ חָמֵ֤שׁ וְתִשְׁעִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֹ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Lemech lived, after he begot Noach, five hundred and ninety-five years,
and he begot sons and daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ כׇּל־יְמֵי־לֶ֔מֶךְ שֶׁ֤בַע וְשִׁבְעִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the days of Lemech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years,
and he died.
And Noach was five hundred years old [(G-d keeping him from begetting until then so that none of his sons reach the (then) age of punishment (100) before the flood.)]
And Noach begot Shem, Cham, and Yafeth [(Shem, the righteous one, born circumcised, the progenitor of Abraham, being mentioned first, though Yefeth was the oldest.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּֽי־הֵחֵ֣ל הָֽאָדָ֔ם לָרֹ֖ב עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה
pairs.english: And it was, when men began to multiply upon the face of the earth
and daughters were born to them,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֤וּ בְנֵי־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֥י טֹבֹ֖ת הֵ֑נָּה
pairs.english: that the sons of the nobles saw the daughters of men when they were adorned [to be wed, at which time one of them cohabited with her first],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נָשִׁ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרוּ׃
pairs.english: and they took for themselves consorts of all that they chose, [even by way of adultery, even by way of sodomy].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהֹוָ֗ה לֹֽא־יָד֨וֹן רוּחִ֤י בָֽאָדָם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said: My spirit shall not contend [in Me] forever [i.e., interminably] concerning man, [whether or not to destroy him,]
in that [this,] too, [is in him, that] he is flesh, [and not a hard substance — and even so he does not humble himself before Me!]
and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years, [at which time, if he has not repented, I shall bring a flood.]

pairs.hebrew: הַנְּפִלִ֞ים הָי֣וּ בָאָ֘רֶץ֮ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֒ וְגַ֣ם אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן
pairs.english: The Nefilim [those who fell (naflu) and who overthrew (hipilu) the world] were in the land in those days [the days of the generation of Enosh and the sons of Cain], and also afterwards [(after they had seen a third of the world flooded in the days of Enosh and should have repented of their ways)],

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבֹ֜אוּ בְּנֵ֤י הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְיָלְד֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: when the sons of the nobles came to (i.e., lived with) the daughters of men, who bore unto them [giants like them].

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֧מָּה הַגִּבֹּרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מֵעוֹלָ֖ם אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַשֵּֽׁם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: They are the "mighty ones" [in rebelling against the L-rd]; of yore, men of name [(their names alluding to their future downfall, e.g., "Irad," "Mechuyael," Methushael" (4:18), all connoting destruction)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא יְהֹוָ֔ה כִּ֥י רַבָּ֛ה רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And the L-rd saw that the evil of man was great in the earth

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־יֵ֙צֶר֙ מַחְשְׁבֹ֣ת לִבּ֔וֹ רַ֥ק רַ֖ע כׇּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day.
And the L-rd was comforted that He had made man on earth, [and not in heaven, where he would have incited the celestial creatures to rebellion],
and He thought to scourge him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶמְחֶ֨ה אֶת־הָאָדָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֙אתִי֙ מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said: I will blot out the man that I have created from off the face of the earth [He is earth and I shall blot him out with water] —
from man until beast [(The beasts, too, had corrupted their ways)] until creeping thing and bird of the heavens;
for I have bethought Myself [of what to do] for having made them.
And Noach found favor
in the eyes of the L-rd.
These are the progeny of Noach.

pairs.hebrew: נֹ֗חַ אִ֥ישׁ צַדִּ֛יק תָּמִ֥ים הָיָ֖ה בְּדֹֽרֹתָ֑יו
pairs.english: [(Noach's name having been mentioned, "The remembrance of the righteous is for blessing," viz.:)] Noach was a righteous man; perfect was he in his generations.
With G-d [i.e., with His support] Noach walked.
And Noach begot three sons:
Shem, Cham, and Yafeth.
And the earth became corrupt [(with illicit relations and idolatry)] before G-d,
and the earth was filled with theft.
And G-d beheld the earth, and, behold, it had become corrupt,
for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth, [even beasts, animals, and birds mating outside of their kind].
And G-d said to Noach:
The end of all flesh has come before Me, [illicit relations and idolatry bringing "promiscuous" destruction to the world],
for the earth is filled with theft through them, [theft "sealing" their decree],
and, behold, I shall destroy them from the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood.
[Measured] compartments shall you make in the ark,
and you shall pitch it inside and outside with pitch [against the turbulent waters].
And this is how you shall make it:

pairs.hebrew: שְׁלֹ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אַמָּ֗ה אֹ֚רֶךְ הַתֵּבָ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ רׇחְבָּ֔הּ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: three hundred cubits, the length of the ark; fifty cubits, its width; and thirty cubits, its height.
A window shall you make for the ark.
To a cubit shall you finish it above, [the roof slanting upwards to a cubit so that the water would run down its sides],
and the door of the ark shall you place in its side, [so that the rain not enter it].
Lower stories [for dung], middle stories [for animals], and third stories [for men] shall you make it.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אֶת־הַמַּבּ֥וּל מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: And, behold, I shall bring the deluge [(in concession to the angels' "What is man that You are mindful of him?")], waters upon the earth,

pairs.hebrew: לְשַׁחֵ֣ת כׇּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ חַיִּ֔ים מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: to destroy all flesh that has in it a spirit of life from under the heavens.
All that is on the earth shall perish.
And I shall establish My covenant with you [(a "covenant" being needed so that the food not decay and so that the wicked ones of the generation not kill him)].
And you shall come to the ark;
you and your sons, and your wife and the wives of your sons with you [(men and women separately, cohabitation being forbidden to them in the ark)].
And of all that lives [(including demons)], of all flesh,

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנַ֧יִם מִכֹּ֛ל תָּבִ֥יא אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֣ת אִתָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: [at least] two [male and female] of all [even of the least numerous] shall you bring to the ark to keep alive with you.
Male and female shall they be.

pairs.hebrew: מֵהָע֣וֹף לְמִינֵ֗הוּ וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ מִכֹּ֛ל רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: Of birds [who had mated] according to their kind [and not promiscuously] and of beasts according to their kind, of all the creeping things of the ground, according to their kind —
two of all shall come to you to keep alive, [(all coming, the ark admitting only those which had mated with their kind, and Noach taking two of these)].
And you, take for yourself
all of the food that is to be eaten, and gather it unto you,
and it shall be for you and for them to eat.
And Noach did [i.e., built]

pairs.hebrew: כְּ֠כֹ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה׃
pairs.english: as all that G-d commanded him; thus did he do.
And the L-rd said to Noach:
Come, you and all your household into the ark;

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: for you have I seen to be righteous before Me in this generation [(as opposed to "perfectly righteous" (6:9), only part of a man's praises being stated to his face)].

pairs.hebrew: מִכֹּ֣ל ׀ הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה תִּֽקַּח־לְךָ֛ שִׁבְעָ֥ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: Of all the beasts that are [destined to be pronounced] clean [to Israel (whence it follows that Noach studied Torah)], take for yourself seven, seven, male and female, [some to be sacrificed upon leaving the ark],

pairs.hebrew: וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֡ה אֲ֠שֶׁ֠ר לֹ֣א טְהֹרָ֥ה הִ֛וא שְׁנַ֖יִם אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and of the beasts which are not clean, two, male and female.

pairs.hebrew: גַּ֣ם מֵע֧וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם שִׁבְעָ֥ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה זָכָ֣ר וּנְקֵבָ֑ה
pairs.english: Also, of the [clean] birds of heaven, seven, seven, male and female,
to sustain seed on the face of all the earth.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ לְיָמִ֨ים ע֜וֹד שִׁבְעָ֗ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מַמְטִ֣יר עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: For in an additional seven days [seven days of mourning in honor of Methuselah, in addition to the 120 year grace period], I shall bring down rain upon the earth,
forty days and forty nights [(retribution for constraining the L-rd to form bastard embryos, (forty days being the formation period)],

pairs.hebrew: וּמָחִ֗יתִי אֶֽת־כׇּל־הַיְקוּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
pairs.english: and I shall blot out every being that I have made from the face of the earth.
And Noach did
as all that the L-rd had commanded him, [in entering the ark].
And Noach was six hundred years old
when the deluge was water upon the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָ֠יו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Noach and his sons, and his wife, and the wives of his sons with him, entered the ark [(men and women separately, cohabitation being forbidden because of the world's affliction)]
in the face of the waters of the deluge, [(even Noach being one of the "small in faith," not entering until actually being "pushed" by the waters)].

pairs.hebrew: מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ הַטְּהוֹרָ֔ה וּמִ֨ן־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֖נָּה טְהֹרָ֑ה
pairs.english: Of the clean beast and of the beast which is not clean
and of the fowl and all that creeps upon the ground.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנַ֨יִם שְׁנַ֜יִם בָּ֧אוּ אֶל־נֹ֛חַ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֖ה זָכָ֣ר וּנְקֵבָ֑ה
pairs.english: Two, two [(at the least)] they came to Noach to the ark, male and female,
as G-d had commanded Noach.
And it was, after the seven days,
that the waters of the deluge were upon the earth.

pairs.hebrew: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי־נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: In the six hundredth year of Noach's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month

pairs.hebrew: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כׇּֽל־מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה
pairs.english: — on this day, all the fountains of the great deep burst,
and the windows of heaven were opened.
And the rain was on the earth
forty days and forty nights [(G-d bringing it down first as "merciful" rain pending their repentance, which, not forthcoming, it was changed to a flood (17)].
On this very day, [in plain sight, in defiance of the wicked ones who said: If we see him entering the ark we will kill him],

pairs.hebrew: בָּ֣א נֹ֔חַ וְשֵׁם־וְחָ֥ם וָיֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וְאֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛יו אִתָּ֖ם אֶל־הַתֵּבָֽה׃
pairs.english: Noach, and Shem, Cham, and Yefeth, the sons of Noach, and the wife of Noach, and the three wives of his sons with them, came to the ark.

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֜מָּה וְכׇל־הַֽחַיָּ֣ה לְמִינָ֗הּ וְכׇל־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְכׇל־הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וְכׇל־הָע֣וֹף לְמִינֵ֔הוּ
pairs.english: They, and every animal according to its kind, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth according to its kind, and every flying thing according to its kind,
every bird of every [type of] wing, [including locusts].
And they came to Noach to the ark,

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנַ֤יִם שְׁנַ֙יִם֙ מִכׇּל־הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ ר֥וּחַ חַיִּֽים׃
pairs.english: two, two, of all flesh which had in it the spirit of life.
And those who came, male and female of all flesh came,
as G-d had commanded him,
and the L-rd closed up [the ark] for him [against the waters].
And the flood was on the earth forty days,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְבּ֣וּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַתָּ֖רׇם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and the waters increased and bore up the ark, and it was lifted above the earth.
And the waters grew stronger and increased greatly upon the earth,
and the ark moved on the face of the waters.
And the waters grew exceedingly stronger upon the earth,
and all the high mountains under all of the heavens were covered.

pairs.hebrew: חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה גָּבְר֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: The waters grew stronger [until they were] fifteen cubits above [the mountains],
and the mountains were covered.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגְוַ֞ע כׇּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר ׀ הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ בָּע֤וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבַ֣חַיָּ֔ה
pairs.english: And all the flesh died that moved upon the ground, in bird, beast, and animal,
and in all creeping things that creep on the ground, and all men (died).
Whatever had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils,
of all that was on the dry land, died, [but not the fish in the sea].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת־כׇּל־הַיְק֣וּם ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד־בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד־רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And He blotted out every being upon the face of the ground — from man until beast until creeping thing until bird of heaven. And they were blotted out from the earth,
and there remained
only Noach
and those with him
in the ark.
And the waters grew stronger upon the earth,
a hundred and fifty days.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כׇּל־הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה
pairs.english: And G-d [(Elokim, the attribute of justice, having been transmuted to that of mercy by Noach's prayers)] remembered Noach and all of the animals, and all of the beasts which were with him in the ark, [G-d "remembering" in their behalf that they had not corrupted their ways (by mating with different species) and that they had not mated in the ark],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֙וּחַ֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and G-d passed [before Him] a spirit [of conciliation and easement] over the ["affairs" of] the earth, and the waters receded.
And the fountains of the deep were dammed up [(not all the fountains as in 7:11; those needed for the continuation of the world were left open)] and the openings of heaven;
and the rain was withheld from the heavens.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב
pairs.english: And the waters started returning from upon the earth,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: and the waters began receding at the end of a hundred and fifty days [on the first of Sivan].
And the ark rested in [Sivan] the seventh month

pairs.hebrew: בְּשִׁבְעָה־עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט׃
pairs.english: [after Kislev, when the rains had stopped falling], on the seventeenth day of the month, on Mount Ararat.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַמַּ֗יִם הָיוּ֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְחָס֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֑י
pairs.english: And the waters kept on receding until [Av] the tenth month [after the beginning of the rain in Marcheshvan].

pairs.hebrew: בָּֽעֲשִׂירִי֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ נִרְא֖וּ רָאשֵׁ֥י הֶֽהָרִֽים׃
pairs.english: In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
And it was at the end of forty days [from when the tops of the mountains were seen]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח נֹ֔חַ אֶת־חַלּ֥וֹן הַתֵּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
pairs.english: that Noach opened the window [i.e., the skylight] of the ark that he had made.
And he sent the raven,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יָצוֹא֙ וָשׁ֔וֹב עַד־יְבֹ֥שֶׁת הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and it went out and circled [(the ark, not executing its mission, suspecting Noach of designs upon its mate)], until the waters had dried off from the earth.
And he sent away the dove from him [after seven days]

pairs.hebrew: לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲקַ֣לּוּ הַמַּ֔יִם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
pairs.english: to see if the waters had "lightened" from the face of the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־מָצְאָה֩ הַיּוֹנָ֨ה מָנ֜וֹחַ לְכַף־רַגְלָ֗הּ וַתָּ֤שׇׁב אֵלָיו֙ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֔ה
pairs.english: And the dove found no rest for the sole of its foot, and it returned to him to the ark,
for waters were on the face of the whole earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־הַתֵּבָֽה׃
pairs.english: And he sent forth his hand and he took it and he brought it to him to the ark.
And he waited yet another seven days,
and he again sent forth the dove from the ark.
And the dove came to him towards evening,
and, behold, it had torn an olive leaf with its beak,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי־קַ֥לּוּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and Noach knew that the waters had lightened from off the earth.
And he held off another seven days,
and he sent the dove, and it did not return to him again.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יְהִ֠י בְּאַחַ֨ת וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֜וֹת שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And it was in the six hundred and first year (of Noach's life), in the first month [of the year], on the first day of the month,
that the water dried from off the earth,
and Noach removed the covering of the ark,
and, behold, the face of the earth had become (somewhat) hardened.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month,

[exactly one solar year after the beginning of the flood (see 7:11), this being the duration of the punishment of the generation of the flood], the earth dried up [i.e., it returned to its normal state].
And G-d spoke
to Noach, saying:
Go out of the ark
— you and your wife, [cohabitation now being permitted (see 7:7)], and your sons and the wives of your sons with you.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַחַיָּ֨ה אֲשֶֽׁר־אִתְּךָ֜ מִכׇּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר בָּע֧וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּבְכׇל־הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ
pairs.english: Every animal that is with you, of all flesh, of bird and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth
haytzeh ["Tell them to go out" (this, the spoken form), or hotzeh, "Take them out" (by force, if they refuse to leave — this, the written form)] with you,
and they shall teem in the earth, [but not in the ark (whence it is seen that even the beasts and the birds were forbidden to mate there)],
and they shall be fruitful and shall multiply upon the earth.
And there went out Noach
and his sons and his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַֽחַיָּ֗ה כׇּל־הָרֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ וְכׇל־הָע֔וֹף כֹּ֖ל רוֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird — every thing that creeps upon the earth,
according to their families [(They took upon themselves to mate only with their kind)]
went out of the ark.
And Noach built an altar to the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל ׀ הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּה֔וֹר
pairs.english: and he took of all the clean beasts and of all the clean birds
and he offered up burnt-offerings upon the altar, [reasoning that he had been commanded to bring "seven, seven" of those (7:2) only so that he might offer sacrifices].
And the L-rd smelled the fragrant odor,
and the L-rd said within His heart:

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־אֹ֠סִ֠ף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם
pairs.english: I shall not again curse the ground for the sake of man.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו
pairs.english: For the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth [(min'eurav, lit., from the time he "bestirs" himself (to leave his mother's womb)],

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת־כׇּל־חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
pairs.english: and I shall not again [(repetition constituting an oath)] smite all living things as I have done.
No more shall cease, all the days of the earth,

pairs.hebrew: זֶ֡רַע וְ֠קָצִ֠יר וְקֹ֨ר וָחֹ֜ם וְקַ֧יִץ וָחֹ֛רֶף
pairs.english: seed-time [half of Tishrei, Marcheshvan, and half of Kislev], and harvest-time [half of Nissan, Iyyar, and half of Sivan], cold-season [half of Kislev, Teveth, and half of Shvat], and hot season [half of Av, Elul, and half of Tishrei], summer-fruit season [half of Sivan, Tammuz, and half of Av], and winter-fruit season [half of Shvat, Adar, and half of Nissan],
and day and night [shall not cease (whence it is seen that all the days of the flood they did cease)].
And G-d blessed Noach and his sons,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and He said to them: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כׇּל־חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כׇּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And your dread and your awe shall be upon all the animals of the earth and on all the birds of the heaven,

pairs.hebrew: בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכׇל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: on all that moves upon the earth and on all the fish of the sea; into your hand are they given.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאׇכְלָ֑ה
pairs.english: Every creeping thing that lives shall be for you to eat.
As green herbs [which alone, I permitted to Adam], to you have I given all.
Only, you shall not eat flesh
with its life [(the ban on ever min hachai — flesh torn from a living animal)] — blood [(the ban on blood from a living animal)].
But [though I have permitted you to take the life of a beast], I shall require your blood [(if you take your life)]

for your lives [even if you do not spill blood, (e.g., strangulation)]. From the hand of every animal will I [now] require it, [the men of the generation of the flood having been consigned as prey to the beasts],

pairs.hebrew: וּמִיַּ֣ד הָֽאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ הָֽאָדָֽם׃
pairs.english: and from the hand of man [one who kills wilfully, in the absence of witnesses], from the hand of a man [against one he loves as] his brother, [whom he kills unwittingly, in the absence of witnesses to make him liable to exile, and in the absence of contrition and penance on his part], I shall require the life of a man.

pairs.hebrew: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הָֽאָדָ֔ם בָּֽאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ
pairs.english: One who spills the blood of man [in the presence of witnesses], by man shall his blood be spilled.
[Why so?] For in the image of G-d did He make man.
And you, be fruitful and multiply, [(this being stated originally (9:1) as a blessing, and here, as a command)],
teem in the earth and increase in it.
And G-d said to Noach and to his sons with him,
saying:
And I, behold, [I concur with you in your apprehension of begetting children (with the threat of another deluge looming over them) and] I am establishing My covenant with you [not to destroy you],
and with your seed after you.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־נֶ֤פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֔ם בָּע֧וֹף בַּבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּֽבְכׇל־חַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ אִתְּכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And with all living things that are with you, of bird and beast, and of all the animals of the earth that are ["compatible"] with you,

pairs.hebrew: מִכֹּל֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י הַתֵּבָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: of all that leave the ark [including reptiles and creeping things], of all the animals of the earth [including mazikkin ("injurers")].
And I will confirm [through the sign of the rainbow] My covenant with you,
and no flesh will again be cut off by the waters of the deluge,
and there will not again be a deluge to destroy the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֗ן בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כׇּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And G-d said: This is the sign of the covenant that I give between Me and you and between every living soul that is with you
for the generations [(doroth, written defective, some generations of righteous men not requiring a sign)] forever.
My bow have I set in the cloud,

pairs.hebrew: וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and it shall be a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.
And it will be, when I "cloud a cloud" upon the earth [i.e., when it enters My mind to bring darkness and destruction to the world],
then the bow will be seen in the cloud.

pairs.hebrew: וְזָכַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כׇּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה בְּכׇל־בָּשָׂ֑ר
pairs.english: And I shall remember My covenant between Me and you and between every living thing of all flesh,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה ע֤וֹד הַמַּ֙יִם֙ לְמַבּ֔וּל לְשַׁחֵ֖ת כׇּל־בָּשָֽׂר׃
pairs.english: and the waters will no more be a deluge to destroy all flesh.
And the bow will be in the cloud
and I will see it,
to remember the eternal covenant
between G-d [Elokim — the Attribute of Justice]
and between every living soul
in all flesh
upon the earth.
And G-d said to Noach [showing him the bow]:
This is the sign of the covenant
that I have established
between Me and between all flesh
that is on the earth.
And the sons of Noach
who went out of the ark
were Shem, Cham, and Yefeth;
and Cham was the father of Canaan [(the relationship being mentioned here to shed light on what is to follow vis-à-vis the cursing of Cham and Canaan)].
These three are the sons of Noach,
and from these did the whole earth spread.
And Noach profaned himself, the lord of the ground,
and he planted a vineyard. [He should have planted something else first.]
And he drank from the wine and he was inebriated
and he uncovered himself in the midst of his tent [ahalo, written "ahalah," an allusion to the ten tribes, called by the name of Shomron (Ahalah), who were exiled because of overindulgence in wine].
And Cham the father of Canaan saw [(Some say Canaan saw and reported it to his father)]
the nakedness of his father [(Some say that he castrated him; others, that he sodomized him)],
and he told his two brothers outside.

And Shem took [(Shem, exerting himself on behalf of the mitzvah more than Yefeth did (for which reason his descendants merited the mitzvah of tzitzith)] and Yefeth, the garment [(for which reason he merited burial for his descendants (Ezekiel 39:11), (the descendants of Cham, who shamed his father, being led in nakedness into exile (Isaiah 20:4)],
and they placed it on the shoulders of both
and they walked backwards,
and they covered the nakedness of their father,
and their faces were [(kept)] turned backwards
[when they drew near him to cover him], and the nakedness of their father they did not see.
And Noach awoke from his wine

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃
pairs.english: and he knew what his "small" [i.e., unworthy, despicable] son had done to him.
And he said: Cursed is Canaan;
a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.
And he said: Blessed is the L-rd, the G-d of Shem,
[who is destined to keep His promise to his (Shem's) seed and give them the land of Canaan], and Canaan will be a servant to him.
G-d will "expand" Yefeth,
but He will dwell in the tents of Shem,
and Canaan will be a servant unto him. [Even after the sons of Shem are exiled, servants will be sold to them from the sons of Canaan.]
And Noach lived after the flood
three hundred and fifty years.
And all the days of Noach
were nine hundred and fifty years,
and he died.
And these are the progeny of the sons of Noach —
Shem, Cham, and Yafeth.
And sons were born to them
after the deluge.
The sons of Yefeth:
Gomer, Magog, Maddai, Yavan, Tuval,
Meshech and Tiras [Persia].
And the sons of Gomer:
Ashkenaz, Rifath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Yavan:
Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these there branched out the islands of the nations in their lands,
each after his tongue,
according to their families in their nations.
And the sons of Cham:
Kush, Mitzrayim, Fut, and Canaan.
And the sons of Kush:
Seva, Chavilah, Savtah, Ra'amah, and Savtecha.
And the sons of Ra'amah: Sheva and Dedan.
And Kush begot Nimrod.
He began to be a mighty one in the earth [to cause all to rebel (nimrod = "Let us rebel") against the Holy One Blessed be He in the counsel of the Tower of Babel)].
He was a "mighty snare" [ensnaring men with his mouth and inciting them to rebel against G-d] before the L-rd ["to His face!"],
wherefore it is said [of such as he]:
"As Nimrod, a mighty snare before the L-rd."

pairs.hebrew: וַתְּהִ֨י רֵאשִׁ֤ית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶ֖רֶךְ וְאַכַּ֣ד וְכַלְנֵ֑ה
pairs.english: And the beginning of his kingdom was Bavel and Erech and Akkad and Kalnah
in the land of Shinar.
Ashur went out of that land [when he saw his sons heeding Nimrod and building the tower in rebellion against the L-rd],
and he built Ninveh, and Rechovoth-Ir, and Kalach.
And Ressen,
between Ninveh and Kalach.
It [Ninveh] is "the great city." [see Jonah (1:2)]
And Mitzrayim begot
Ludim
and Anamim
and Lehavim [so called because of their fiery faces (lahav = flame)]
and Naftuchim.
And Patrusim and Kashluchim,
whence came forth
Plishtim
and Kaftorim [Patrusim and Kasluchim "exchanging" their wives, and "between both" begetting Plishtim and Kaftorim].
And Canaan begot
Tziddon, his first-born,
and Cheth.
And the Yevussi
and the Emori
and the Girgashi.
And the Chivi
and the Arki
and the Sini.
And the Arvadi and the Tzemari and the Chamathi.
And after, [from these] there spread forth [many]
families of the Canaani.
And the border of the Canaani
was from Tziddon as you come to Gerar, until Azzah;
as you come to Sodom and Amorrah and Admah and Tzvoyim,
until Lasha.
These are the sons of Cham
according to their families. [(They are all sons of Cham, even though they branched out)]
according to their tongues, in their lands, and in their nations.
And to Shem was born, he too,
the father of all the children of Ever, [(i.e., Shem was the father of all the children of ever hanahar (the other side of the Euphrates)],
the brother of Yefeth, the elder [(Cham not being mentioned in that he, unlike Shem and Yefeth, did not honor his father)].
The sons of Shem:
Eilam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
And the sons of Aram:
Utz, Chul, Gether, and Mash.
And Arpachshad begot
Shalach,
and Shelach begot
Ever.
And to Ever was born two sons;
the name of the first, Peleg,
for in his days the earth was divided (niflegah) [Languages were confounded and men "divided themselves" throughout the earth],
and the name of his brother was Yaktan. [(Because he "humbled" (hiktin) himself, he merited the many families (which follow).]
And Yaktan begot
Almodad, and Shalef, and Chatzarmaveth, and Yarach.
And Hadoram,
and Uzzal,
and Diklah.
And Oval,
and Avimael,
and Sheva.
And Ofir, and Chavilah, and Yovav
—- all these are the sons of Yaktan.
And their habitation was from Mesha,
as you come to Sefar,
a mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem
by their families according to their tongues,
in their lands according to their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noach,
their progeny according to their nations.

pairs.hebrew: וּמֵאֵ֜לֶּה נִפְרְד֧וּ הַגּוֹיִ֛ם בָּאָ֖רֶץ אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And from these there branched out the nations of the earth after the deluge.
And all the earth
was one language [the holy tongue]
and single speech [i.e., united counsel].
And it was, when they traveled from the east [(see 10:30) to find a place that would contain them all]
that they found a valley in the land of Shinar
and they settled there.
And one [nation] said to the other:
Ready yourselves. Let us make bricks, [there being no stone in Bavel (which is a valley)], and let us fire them [in an oven].
And they had brick for stone,
and bitumen for mortar [for wall plaster].
And they said: Let us build for ourselves a city
and a tower with its top in the heavens,
and let us make a name for ourselves
lest we be scattered [by an act of Heaven] upon the face of all the earth.
And the L-rd "went down to see"
[(an object lesson to judges: that they not judge until they see and understand)] the city and the tower
which the sons of [ungrateful] man [whom He had rescued from the flood] had built.
And the L-rd said:

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֣ן עַ֤ם אֶחָד֙ וְשָׂפָ֤ה אַחַת֙ לְכֻלָּ֔ם
pairs.english: Behold, [all of this good is theirs:] they are one people, and all of them have one language,
and this is what they begin to do!
And now, should there not be withheld from them
all that they scheme to do!
Let us [G-d and the celestial tribunal (G-d, in His great humility, including them with Him)] ("Let us") go down ["measure for measure" for "Let us build" (4)] and confound there their language,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפַ֥ת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
pairs.english: that one man not understand another's tongue [and discord result].
And the L-rd scattered them from there
[in this world ("measure for measure" for (4) "lest we be scattered")] on the face of all the earth,
and they ceased building the city.
Therefore, it is called Bavel;
for there the L-rd confounded (balal) the language of all the earth,
and from there the L-rd scattered them [(their having no portion in the world to come)] on the face of all the earth.
These are the progeny of Shem.
Shem was a hundred years old
when he begot Arpachshad
two years after the deluge.
And Shem lived after he begot Arpachshad,
five hundred years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Arpachshad lived
thirty-five years
and he begot Shalach.
And Arpachshad lived after he begot Shelach
four hundred and three years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Shelach lived
thirty years
and he begot Ever.
And Shelach lived after he begot Ever
four hundred and three years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Ever lived
thirty-four years
and he begot Paleg.
And Ever lived after he begot Peleg
four hundred and thirty years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived
thirty years
and he begot Re'u.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְחִי־פֶ֗לֶג אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־רְע֔וּ תֵּ֥שַׁע שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Peleg lived after he begot Re'u, two hundred and nine years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Re'u lived
thirty-two years
and he begot Serug.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֣י רְע֗וּ אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־שְׂר֔וּג שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Re'u lived after he begot Serug two hundred and seven years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Serug lived
thirty years
and he begot Nachor.
And Serug lived after he begot Nachor
two hundred years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Nachor lived
twenty-nine years
and he begot Terach.
And Nachor lived after he begot Terach
a hundred and nineteen years,
and he begot sons and daughters.
And Terach lived
seventy years
and he begot Avram, Nachor, and Haran.
And these are the progeny of Terach:
Terach begot Avram, Nachor and Haran,
and Haran begot Lot.
And Haran died in the lifetime of Terach his father,
in the land of his birth, Ur Kasdim.
And Avram and Nachor took for themselves wives.

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁ֤ם אֵֽשֶׁת־אַבְרָם֙ שָׂרָ֔י וְשֵׁ֤ם אֵֽשֶׁת־נָחוֹר֙ מִלְכָּ֔ה
pairs.english: The name of the wife of Avram was Sarai, and the name of the wife of Nachor was Milkah,

the daughter of Haran, the father of Milkah and the father of Yiskah [Sarah, so called: because she "looked" (sachah) through the Holy Spirit, because all "gazed" at her beauty, and because of her queenly grace (nesichuth)]
And Sarai was barren;
she had no child.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח תֶּ֜רַח אֶת־אַבְרָ֣ם בְּנ֗וֹ וְאֶת־ל֤וֹט בֶּן־הָרָן֙ בֶּן־בְּנ֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ שָׂרַ֣י כַּלָּת֔וֹ אֵ֖שֶׁת אַבְרָ֣ם בְּנ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Terach took Avram, his son, and Lot, the son of Haran, his son's son, and Sarai, his daughter-in-law, the wife of Avram, his son,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ אִתָּ֜ם מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן
pairs.english: and they [Terach and Avram] went out with them [Lot and Sarai] from Ur Kasdim to go to the land of Canaan;
and they came until Charan and they dwelt there.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵי־תֶ֔רַח חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the days of Terach were two hundred and five years,

and Terach "died" in Charan, [the wicked, even in their lifetimes being called "dead" (Scripture stating this here so that Avram's leaving Charan not be felt as a breach of the honor due his father)].
And the L-rd said to Avram:
Go, for your sake, [for your benefit and for your good], from your land and from your birthplace, and from your father's house,
to the land that I will show you.
And I shall make of you a great nation,
and I shall bless you [with wealth],
and I shall make your name great,
and you shall be a [source of] blessing.
And I shall bless those who bless you,
and those who curse you shall I curse,
and they shall bless themselves in you [i.e., in your name] all the families of the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אַבְרָ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Avram went as the L-rd spoke to him,
and Lot went with him.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַבְרָ֗ם בֶּן־חָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּצֵאת֖וֹ מֵחָרָֽן׃
pairs.english: And Avram was seventy-five years old when he went out of Charan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אַבְרָם֩ אֶת־שָׂרַ֨י אִשְׁתּ֜וֹ וְאֶת־ל֣וֹט בֶּן־אָחִ֗יו וְאֶת־כׇּל־רְכוּשָׁם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָכָ֔שׁוּ
pairs.english: And Avram took Sarai, his wife, and Lot, his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered,
and the souls [i.e., bondsmen and bondswomen] that they had acquired in Charan,
and they went out to go to the land of Canaan,
and they came to the land of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אַבְרָם֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ עַ֚ד מְק֣וֹם שְׁכֶ֔ם עַ֖ד אֵל֣וֹן מוֹרֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And Avram passed through the land until the place of Shechem, until Eilon Moreh.
And the Canaanite was then in the land, [conquering Eretz Yisrael from the seed of Shem].
And the L-rd appeared to Avram
and He said:
To your seed shall I give this land.
And he built there [for the tidings of the seed and of the land] an altar
to the L-rd,
who had appeared to him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעְתֵּ֨ק מִשָּׁ֜ם הָהָ֗רָה מִקֶּ֛דֶם לְבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וַיֵּ֣ט אׇהֳלֹ֑ה בֵּֽית־אֵ֤ל מִיָּם֙ וְהָעַ֣י מִקֶּ֔דֶם
pairs.english: And he removed from there [his tent] to the mountain east of Bethel. And he pitched his tent, [first Sarai's, then his], Bethel on the west and Ai on the east.
And he built there an altar to the L-rd, [perceiving prophetically that his children would go astray there by the sin of Achan (Joshua 7)],
and he called, [interceding for them] in the name of the L-rd.
And Avram journeyed
progressively southwards, [towards Jerusalem].
And there was a famine in the land [of Canaan, whither G-d had bidden him go — the L-rd testing Avram],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨רֶד אַבְרָ֤ם מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and Avram went down to Egypt to dwell there, for the famine was sore in the land.
And it was, as he approached Egypt,
that he said to Sarai his wife:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִשָּׁ֥ה יְפַת־מַרְאֶ֖ה אָֽתְּ׃
pairs.english: Behold, now [the time has come to worry about your beauty.] I have long known you to be a beautiful woman.
And it will be, when the Egyptians see you,
that they will say: "This is his wife!"
and they will kill me and keep you alive.
Say, now, that you are my sister,
so that it be well for me for your sake [i.e., so that they give me gifts],
and so that I remain alive because of you.
And it was, when Avram came to Egypt, [with Sarai hidden in a chest]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֤וּ הַמִּצְרִים֙ אֶת־הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־יָפָ֥ה הִ֖וא מְאֹֽד׃
pairs.english: that the Egyptians spied the woman and found her to be very beautiful.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֹתָהּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיְהַֽלְל֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And the officers of Pharaoh saw her, and they praised her [among themselves] as being for Pharaoh;
and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
And he [Pharaoh] benefitted Avram for her sake,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ צֹאן־וּבָקָר֙ וַחֲמֹרִ֔ים וַעֲבָדִים֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וַאֲתֹנֹ֖ת וּגְמַלִּֽים׃
pairs.english: and he had flocks and herds, and he-asses, and bondsmen and bondswomen, and she-asses and camels.
And the L-rd plagued Pharaoh with great afflictions, as well as [the people of] his house,
at the behest of Sarai, Avram's wife.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ לְאַבְרָ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֑י
pairs.english: And Pharaoh called to Avram and he said: What is this that you have done to me?

pairs.hebrew: לָ֚מָּה לֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י כִּ֥י אִשְׁתְּךָ֖ הִֽוא׃
pairs.english: Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?

pairs.hebrew: לָמָ֤ה אָמַ֙רְתָּ֙ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֔וא וָאֶקַּ֥ח אֹתָ֛הּ לִ֖י לְאִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: Why did you say "She is my sister," so that I took her for me as a wife?
And now, here is your wife. Take her and go [out of Egypt (for the Egyptians are licentious)].
And Pharaoh appointed men for him [to guard him],
and they escorted him and his wife and all that was his.
And Avram went up from Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: ה֠וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וְל֥וֹט עִמּ֖וֹ הַנֶּֽגְבָּה׃
pairs.english: he and his wife and all that was with him, and Lot with him to the south [of Eretz Yisrael].
And Avram
was very heavy, with kine, with silver and with gold.

And he went on his travels, [from Egypt, stopping in the same inns as when he had journeyed there (whence we derive that one should not vary his lodgings)] from the south [Egypt being south of Canaan] until Bethel,

pairs.hebrew: עַד־הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֤ם אׇֽהֳלֹה֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה בֵּ֥ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל וּבֵ֥ין הָעָֽי׃
pairs.english: until the place where his tent was in the beginning, between Bethel and Ai.
To the place of the altar which he had made there at first,
where Avram had called upon the name of the L-rd.
And also unto Lot, who went with Avram [— because he went with Avram]
there were flocks and herds, and tents.
And the [pasturage of the] land did not suffice for them
to dwell together,
for their substance was great,
and they could not dwell together.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־רִ֗יב בֵּ֚ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵֽה־אַבְרָ֔ם וּבֵ֖ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵה־ל֑וֹט
pairs.english: And there was a dispute between Avram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen

[the former rebuking the latter for allowing their flocks to graze in others' fields, the latter arguing that there was no theft in this in that the land belonged to Lot, Avram's sole heir.] But [(states Scripture)] the Canaani and the Perizi
then dwelt in the land, [so that Avram not yet having taken possession of the land, the practice of Lot's herdsmen did, indeed, constitute theft.]
And Avram said to Lot:

pairs.hebrew: אַל־נָ֨א תְהִ֤י מְרִיבָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּבֵ֥ין רֹעַ֖י וּבֵ֣ין רֹעֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: Let there not be a dispute between me and you, and between my herdsmen and yours,
for we are kinsmen.
Is not the whole land before you?
Part, I pray you, from me.
If you go to the left, I will be at your right [to defend you]; and if you go to the right, I will be at your left.
And Lot lifted his eyes
and saw the whole plain of the Jordan,
it being all watered [with streams].
Before the L-rd destroyed Sodom and Amorah,
it was like the Garden of the L-rd, like the land of Egypt
[for sowing] until Tzoar.
And Lot chose for himself the entire plain of the Jordan,
and Lot traveled from the east [of Avram, going west],
and they parted, one from the other.
Avram dwelt in the land of Canaan,
and Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain,
and he pitched tents [for his herdsmen and his herds] until Sodom.
And the people of Sodom were evil [with their bodies] and sinful [with their wealth]
to the L-rd exceedingly, [in spite of which Lot did not forbear living among them].
