pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Avram after Lot departed from him [(the Word not coming to him so long as that evil one was with him)]:
Raise your eyes, now, and see,
from the place where you are —
north, south, east, and west.
For all the land that you see,
to you shall I give it, and to your seed forever.
And I shall make your seed as the dust of the earth —

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ אִם־יוּכַ֣ל אִ֗ישׁ לִמְנוֹת֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: so that just as the dust of the earth cannot be counted,
so your seed will not be counted.
Arise, walk in the land, in its length and its breadth,
for to you shall I give it.
And Avram pitched his tent,
and he came and he dwelt
in the plains of [the man] Mamre,
in Chevron,
and he built there an altar
to the L-rd.
And it was in the days of Amrafel [Nimrod (10:8-9)], king of Shinar;
Aryoch, king of Elassar;
Kedarlaomer, king of Elam;
and Tidal, king of Goyim, [a place so called because many nations (goyim) gathered there],
that they made war

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־בֶּ֙רַע֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ סְדֹ֔ם וְאֶת־בִּרְשַׁ֖ע מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמֹרָ֑ה
pairs.english: with Bera ["evil" (to Heaven and evil to man)], king of Sodom; Birsha [(ascending "in wickedness")], king of Amorah;
Shinav ["hating his Father" (in heaven)], king of Admah; Shemever ["took wing" (to rebel against the L-rd)], king of Tzvoyim,
and the king of Bela, which is [the city of] Tzoar.
All of these joined together in the valley of Siddim ["many fields"],
which is [now] the Salt Sea, [the waters having spilled into it].
Twelve years they [these five kings] served Kedarlaomer,
and for thirteen years, they rebelled.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה בָּ֣א כְדׇרְלָעֹ֗מֶר וְהַמְּלָכִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: And in the fourteenth year [of their rebellion], Kedarlaomer came and the kings who were with him, [the other three],
and they smote Refaim in Ashteroth Karnayim,
the Zuzim [same as Zamzumim (Deuteronomy 2:10)] in Ham,
and the Eimim in Shaveh Kiryathaim.
And the Chori, in their mountain, Seir,
until El [the plain of] Paran, which is near the desert.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יָּשֻׁ֠בוּ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־עֵ֤ין מִשְׁפָּט֙ הִ֣וא קָדֵ֔שׁ
pairs.english: And they returned and they came to Ein Mishpat ["the spring of judgment" (so called because Moses and Aaron were destined to be judged there regarding the spring (Numbers 20:1 and 14)], which is Kadesh,
and they smote the entire field of the Amaleki [so called in terms of the future, (Amalek not having yet been born)],
and also the Emori, who dwelt in Chatzatzon Tamar [Ein Gedi].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹ֜ם וּמֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמֹרָ֗ה וּמֶ֤לֶךְ אַדְמָה֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ (צביים) [צְבוֹיִ֔ם] וּמֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּ֖לַע הִוא־צֹ֑עַר
pairs.english: And there went out the king of Sodom and the king of Amorah and the king of Admah and the king of Tzvoyim and the king of Bela, which is Tzoar,
and they waged war against them in the valley of Siddim.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת כְּדׇרְלָעֹ֜מֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ עֵילָ֗ם וְתִדְעָל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְאַמְרָפֶל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ שִׁנְעָ֔ר וְאַרְי֖וֹךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶלָּסָ֑ר
pairs.english: Kedarlaomer, king of Elam; Tidal, king of Goyim; Amrafel, king of Shinar; Aryoch, king of Elassar —
four kings against the five, [in spite of which the former were victorious (a tribute to Avram's subsequent vanquishing of them)].
And the valley of Siddim was full of bitumen pits,
and the king of Sodom and Amorah fled and fell there,
and those that remained fled to a mountain.
And they took all the wealth of Sodom and Amorah and all of their food
and they went.
And they took Lot and his wealth, the son of Avram's brother,
and they went.
And he sat in Sodom. [What was the cause of his being despoiled? His sitting in Sodom.]
And the survivor came, [Og, who had escaped from the battle (see Deuteronomy 3:11)],
and he told Avram the Ivri, [from ever (the other side of) the river (Euphrates)];
and he lived in the plains of Mamre, the Emori,
the brother of Eshkol and the brother of Aner,
who had made a covenant with Avram.
And Avram heard that his brother had been taken captive,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨רֶק אֶת־חֲנִיכָ֜יו יְלִידֵ֣י בֵית֗וֹ שְׁמֹנָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת
pairs.english: and he spurred his novices, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen,
and he pursued them until Dan, [his strength waning there (Avram seeing, prophetically, that his descendants were destined to erect the image of a calf there)].
And he and his servants divided [themselves] against them at night, and he pursued them until Chovah,
[Dan, so called because of its guilt (chov), idolatry], which was to the left of Damascus.
And he returned all of the wealth,
and also Lot, his brother, and his wealth he returned,
and also the women and the people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹם֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒ אַחֲרֵ֣י שׁוּב֗וֹ מֵֽהַכּוֹת֙ אֶת־כְּדׇרְלָעֹ֔מֶר וְאֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the king of Sodom went out towards him after he returned from smiting Kedarlaomer and the kings who were with him,
to the valley of Shaveh, the king's vale [his race-course].

pairs.hebrew: וּמַלְכִּי־צֶ֙דֶק֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ שָׁלֵ֔ם הוֹצִ֖יא לֶ֣חֶם וָיָ֑יִן
pairs.english: And Malkitzedek, the king of Shalem, brought out bread and wine [(standing fare for the battle-weary),
Malkitzedek demonstrating thereby that he bore Avram no malice for having killed his sons.] And he was a Cohein to G-d on High.
And he blessed him and said:

pairs.hebrew: בָּר֤וּךְ אַבְרָם֙ לְאֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן קֹנֵ֖ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: Blessed is Avram to G-d on High, Possessor of heaven and earth, [having acquired them by creating them].

pairs.hebrew: וּבָרוּךְ֙ אֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־מִגֵּ֥ן צָרֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And blessed is G-d on High, who has delivered your foes into your hand.
And he (Avram) gave him a tithe of all, [Malkitzedek being a Cohein].
And the king of Sodom said to Avram:
Give me the souls [from the spoils taken of me, which you have rescued], and the wealth take for yourself.
And Avram said to the king of Sodom:

pairs.hebrew: הֲרִמֹ֨תִי יָדִ֤י אֶל־יְהֹוָה֙ אֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן קֹנֵ֖ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: I lift my hand [in oath] to the L-rd, G-d on High, Possessor of heaven and earth,
Nothing — from a thread until a sandal latchet [shall I keep for myself],
nor shall I take [from your treasure house, if you would offer it to me,] anything that is yours,
so that you not say: "I made Avram rich" [for the L-rd promised to make me rich (12:2)]
Except what the youths have eaten,

pairs.hebrew: וְחֵ֙לֶק֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלְכ֖וּ אִתִּ֑י עָנֵר֙ אֶשְׁכֹּ֣ל וּמַמְרֵ֔א הֵ֖ם יִקְח֥וּ חֶלְקָֽם׃ {ס}
pairs.english: and the portion of the men [my bondsmen], who went with me [to do battle, and] Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre, [who guarded the baggage] — they shall take their portion.

pairs.hebrew: אַחַ֣ר ׀ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם בַּֽמַּחֲזֶ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: After these things, [the miracles wrought for him in vanquishing the kings, (Avram worrying that he might thereby have received his full reward)], the word of the L-rd came to Avram in a vision, saying:
Do not fear, Avram; I am a shield [against punishment] for you [for the men that you have killed; and, as to your concern over having received your full reward],
your reward is extremely great.
And Avram said: L-rd G-d, what will You give me?
I go wasted, [without children],
and the purveyor of my household, [who would otherwise, be my son,] is Eliezer of Damascus.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָ֔ם הֵ֣ן לִ֔י לֹ֥א נָתַ֖תָּה זָ֑רַע
pairs.english: And Avram said: Behold, to me You have not given seed.
[Of what avail, then, is all You have given me], when the son of my household [Eliezer] shall inherit me?
And, behold, the word of the L-rd (came) to him, saying:
This one shall not inherit you,

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־אִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִמֵּעֶ֔יךָ ה֖וּא יִֽירָשֶֽׁךָ׃
pairs.english: but one who issues from your loins — he will inherit you.
And He took him outside [of his tent],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַבֶּט־נָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יְמָה וּסְפֹר֙ הַכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים אִם־תּוּכַ֖ל לִסְפֹּ֣ר אֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: and He said: Look, now, heavenwards, and count the stars if you can count them.
And He said to him: Thus shall be your seed.
And he believed in the L-rd, [not asking a sign for this as he did for the inheritance of the land (8)],
and He accounted it [his not asking for a sign] unto him as righteousness.
And He said to him:

pairs.hebrew: אֲנִ֣י יְהֹוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵאתִ֙יךָ֙ מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים
pairs.english: I am the L-rd who took you out of Ur Kasdim
to give you this land to inherit it.
And he said:

pairs.hebrew: אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהֹוִ֔ה בַּמָּ֥ה אֵדַ֖ע כִּ֥י אִֽירָשֶֽׁנָּה׃
pairs.english: O L-rd, G-d, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?
And He said to him:

pairs.hebrew: קְחָ֥ה לִי֙ עֶגְלָ֣ה מְשֻׁלֶּ֔שֶׁת וְעֵ֥ז מְשֻׁלֶּ֖שֶׁת וְאַ֣יִל מְשֻׁלָּ֑שׁ
pairs.english: Take for Me three heifers, [intimating three bullocks: the bullock of Yom Kippur, the bullock of communal forgetfulness (Leviticus 4:13), and the bullock of the broken neck (Deuteronomy 21:4)], and three goats, [intimating the goat offered within (the holy of holies), the additional Festival goats, and the sin-offering goat of the individual (as opposed to that of the congregation)], and three rams, [intimating the confirmed guilt-offering, the suspended guilt-offering, and the sin-offering ewe of the individual],
and a turtle-dove and a young pigeon.
And he took unto Him all these, [(the bullocks, rams, and goats, representing the nations; and the young doves, Israel)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְבַתֵּ֤ר אֹתָם֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אִישׁ־בִּתְר֖וֹ לִקְרַ֣את רֵעֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: and he split them [it being the custom of those entering into a covenant to split a beast and walk through the pieces, (G-d and Avram entering into a covenant here for Israel's inheritance of the land)], (… and he split them) in the middle, [(a sign that the nations would be destroyed)]. And he placed each piece opposite the other;
but the birds he did not split [(a sign that Israel would remain "intact")].
And (predatory) birds swooped down upon the [pieces of the] carcasses,
and Avram swept them away [(a sign that David the son of Yishai will seek to destroy them (the nations), but will not be permitted to do so, until the advent of the Messiah.)]
And the sun was about to set
when a great sleep fell over Avram,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵימָ֛ה חֲשֵׁכָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה נֹפֶ֥לֶת עָלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and behold, a great dark fright [(intimating the woes and darkness of Israel's exiles)] descended upon him.
And He said to Avram: Know shall you know

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־גֵ֣ר ׀ יִהְיֶ֣ה זַרְעֲךָ֗ בְּאֶ֙רֶץ֙ לֹ֣א לָהֶ֔ם
pairs.english: that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs,

pairs.hebrew: וַעֲבָד֖וּם וְעִנּ֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: and they shall serve them and they shall afflict them, four hundred years [(from the birth of Isaac until the exodus)].
And also [(including the four kingdoms)] the nation that they shall serve
will I judge [with ten plagues],
and afterwards they shall leave with great wealth [see Exodus 12:36].
And you will come to your fathers [(Terach repented of his idolatry)] in peace [not witnessing any of the above].
You will be buried in a good old age, [Ishmael repenting and Esav not turning to evil in his days].
And the fourth generation [of the Egyptian exile] shall return here [to Canaan (e.g., Calev, the son of Chetzron, the son of Peretz, the son of Judah was among those entering the land)],
for the sin of the Emori would not have been consummated, [(justifying their being driven out of the land)] until then.
And it was, when the sun had set and it was dark,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֨ה תַנּ֤וּר עָשָׁן֙ וְלַפִּ֣יד אֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֔ר בֵּ֖ין הַגְּזָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
pairs.english: and, behold, a smoking furnace and a torch of fire that passed between these pieces [(intimating the descent of the kingdoms into Gehinnom)].

pairs.hebrew: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא כָּרַ֧ת יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־אַבְרָ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: On that day the L-rd made a covenant with Avram, saying:

pairs.hebrew: לְזַרְעֲךָ֗ נָתַ֙תִּי֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את מִנְּהַ֣ר מִצְרַ֔יִם עַד־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל נְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃
pairs.english: To your seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt until the Great River, the Euphrates [(called the "Great river" because of its being mentioned in conjunction with Eretz Yisrael)].
The Keini and the Kenizi
and the Kadmoni.
And the Chitti and the Perizi
and the Refaim.
And the Emori
and the Canaani
and the Girgashi

and the Yevussi, [ten nations all told, although only seven were conquered. The Keini, the Kenizi, and the Kadmoni (Edom, Moav, and Ammon) were destined to be inherited in time to come (Isaiah 11:4)].

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׂרַי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת אַבְרָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָלְדָ֖ה ל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Sarai the wife of Avram had not borne (children) unto him.
And she had an Egyptian handmaid [the daughter of Pharaoh], whose name was Hagar.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֜י אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם הִנֵּה־נָ֞א עֲצָרַ֤נִי יְהֹוָה֙ מִלֶּ֔דֶת
pairs.english: And Sarai said to Avram: Behold, the L-rd has held me back from bearing.
Come, I pray you, to my handmaid. Perhaps I will be built up through her [in the merit of bringing my rival into my house].
And Avram heeded the voice [the Holy spirit] of Sarai.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּ֞ח שָׂרַ֣י אֵֽשֶׁת־אַבְרָ֗ם אֶת־הָגָ֤ר הַמִּצְרִית֙ שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ
pairs.english: And Sarai the wife of Avram "took" [by suasion] Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid,

pairs.hebrew: מִקֵּץ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר שָׁנִ֔ים לְשֶׁ֥בֶת אַבְרָ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: after ten years [(this being the mandatory period for taking a new wife after a childless union)] of Avram's dwelling in the land of Canaan [(the years outside the land of Canaan being irrelevant in this regard)],

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְאַבְרָ֥ם אִישָׁ֖הּ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
pairs.english: and she gave her to Avram her husband as a wife.
And he came to Hagar and she conceived [from the first union].

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וַתֵּקַ֥ל גְּבִרְתָּ֖הּ בְּעֵינֶֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: And when she saw that she had [thus] conceived, her mistress became light in her eyes [by invidious comparison].
And Sarai said to Avram: [The punishment for] my being wronged is upon you [for having prayed that you (not necessarily I) be granted children].

pairs.hebrew: אָנֹכִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּי שִׁפְחָתִי֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וָאֵקַ֖ל בְּעֵינֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: I gave my handmaid into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived I became light in her eyes.
May the L-rd judge between me and you.
And Avram said to Sarai:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה שִׁפְחָתֵךְ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔ךְ עֲשִׂי־לָ֖הּ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יִךְ
pairs.english: Behold, your handmaid is in your hand. Do with her as is good in your eyes.
And Sarai afflicted her [with arduous labor] and she fled from her presence.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּמְצָאָ֞הּ מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהֹוָ֛ה עַל־עֵ֥ין הַמַּ֖יִם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: And an angel of the L-rd found her by a well of water in the desert,
by the well on the way to Shur.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר הָגָ֞ר שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרַ֛י אֵֽי־מִזֶּ֥ה בָ֖את וְאָ֣נָה תֵלֵ֑כִי
pairs.english: And he said: Hagar, handmaid of Sarai, whence do you come and whither are you going?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִפְּנֵי֙ שָׂרַ֣י גְּבִרְתִּ֔י אָנֹכִ֖י בֹּרַֽחַת׃
pairs.english: And she said: I am fleeing Sarai my mistress.
And an angel of the L-rd said to her [(a different angel being sent for each "saying")]:
Return to your mistress and be afflicted under her hands.
And an angel of the L-rd said to her:

pairs.hebrew: הַרְבָּ֥ה אַרְבֶּ֖ה אֶת־זַרְעֵ֑ךְ וְלֹ֥א יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃
pairs.english: I shall multiply your seed, and they shall not be counted for multitude.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן
pairs.english: And an angel of the L-rd said to her: Behold, you shall conceive [(her first conception having been aborted by Sarai's "evil eye")], and you will bear a son;

pairs.hebrew: וְקָרָ֤את שְׁמוֹ֙ יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֥ע יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־עׇנְיֵֽךְ׃
pairs.english: and call his name Ishmael, for G-d [El] has given heed [shama] to your afflictions.

pairs.hebrew: וְה֤וּא יִהְיֶה֙ פֶּ֣רֶא אָדָ֔ם יָד֣וֹ בַכֹּ֔ל וְיַ֥ד כֹּ֖ל בּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And he will be a man of the wilderness, his hand against all [i.e., a robber] and the hand of all against him, [hating him and assailing him],
and on the face of his brothers shall he dwell, [his seed being numerous].
And she called the name of the L-rd who spoke to her
"You are the G-d of seeing";
for she said:
Would I have believed to see [an angel of the L-rd] here [in the wilderness], too, after having seen (angels) [in the house of Avram]?

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּן֙ קָרָ֣א לַבְּאֵ֔ר בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י
pairs.english: She, therefore, called the well "the well of the appearance of the living (angel)."
It is between Kadesh and Bared.
And Hagar bore a son to Avram.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָ֧ם שֶׁם־בְּנ֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה הָגָ֖ר יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל׃
pairs.english: And Avram called [through the Holy Spirit] the name of his son, whom Hagar had borne, "Ishmael."
And Avram was eighty-six years old
when Hagar bore Ishmael to Avram [(this being mentioned to Ishmael's credit, that though thirteen years old when circumcised, (17:24-25), he did not protest)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י אַבְרָ֔ם בֶּן־תִּשְׁעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְתֵ֣שַׁע שָׁנִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Avram was ninety-nine years old,
and the L-rd appeared to Avram and He said to him:
I am the All-Sufficient G-d.
[Therefore,] walk before Me [i.e., worship Me] and be whole [in the trials I shall set for you, and I shall be your Patron].
And I shall set My covenant [of love and of inheritance of the land (through the mitzvah of circumcision)] between Me and you,
and I will increase you exceedingly.
And Avram fell upon his face [in awe, lacking the power to stand in the presence of the Shechinah while yet uncircumcised].
And the L-rd spoke to him, saying:
I, behold, My covenant is with you,
and you shall be the father of a multitude of nations.
And your name will no longer be called Avram,
but your name will be Avraham,
for a father of a multitude (av hamon) of nations have I made you [("Av (ra) ham," acronymically = av hamon)]
And I shall multiply you exceedingly,
and I shall make of you nations [Israel and Edom, (Ishmael already having been born)],
and kings will go forth from you.

pairs.hebrew: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֜י בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֗ךָ וּבֵ֨ין זַרְעֲךָ֧ אַחֲרֶ֛יךָ לְדֹרֹתָ֖ם לִבְרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations as an eternal covenant,
[My covenant being] to be a G-d unto you and unto your seed after you.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְ֠ךָ֠ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֨ אַחֲרֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת ׀ אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֗יךָ אֵ֚ת כׇּל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן לַאֲחֻזַּ֖ת עוֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: And I will give unto you and unto your seed after you the land of your sojournings, the whole land of Canaan, as an eternal holding,
and [there] I will be a G-d unto them [(but if one lives elsewhere, it is "as if he has no G-d")].
And G-d said to Abraham:

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֣י תִשְׁמֹ֑ר אַתָּ֛ה וְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַֽחֲרֶ֖יךָ לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: And, [as for] you, My covenant shall you keep, you and your seed after you throughout your generations.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁמְר֗וּ בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: [And what constitutes its "keeping"?] This is My covenant which you shall keep between Me and you [those living now] and your seed after you, [those yet to be born]
— that all of your males be circumcised.
And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskins,
and it shall be for a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

pairs.hebrew: וּבֶן־שְׁמֹנַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יִמּ֥וֹל לָכֶ֛ם כׇּל־זָכָ֖ר לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And at eight days old, every male of yours throughout your generations shall be circumcised,

pairs.hebrew: יְלִ֣יד בָּ֔יִת וּמִקְנַת־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ מִכֹּ֣ל בֶּן־נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹ֥א מִֽזַּרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: (whether) born at home [of your maidservant] or bought for money [after he was born] of any stranger who is not of your seed.
Circumcised, he shall be circumcised, [in any event, even (in certain cases) after eight days], one born in your house and one bought for your money,
and My covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָרֵ֣ל ׀ זָכָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִמּוֹל֙ אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר עׇרְלָת֔וֹ וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּ֑יהָ
pairs.english: And an uncircumcised male [(the locus of circumcision being the "maleness" locus)], who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin [upon reaching the age of liability] — that soul shall be cut off from its people, [going childless and dying before his time. (But if his father is remiss in circumcising him, he is in transgression of a positive commandment, but does not incur "cutting off")];
My covenant has he broken.
And G-d said to Abraham:
Sarai your wife — you shall not call her name Sarai ["my mistress"];
but her name is Sarah ["mistress (over all)"].
And I shall bless her, [rejuvenating her (18:12)],
and I shall also give from her to you a son,
and I shall bless her [with nursing breasts], and nations will issue from her;
kings of peoples will come from her.
And Abraham fell upon his face and he rejoiced.
And he said in his heart:
Would [anyone think that] a man of a hundred [would] beget!
or that Sarah, a woman of ninety, would bear!
And Abraham said to G-d:
Would that Ishmael lived before You [i.e., worshipping You]!
And G-d said:
In truth, Sarah your wife

pairs.hebrew: יֹלֶ֤דֶת לְךָ֙ בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יִצְחָ֑ק
pairs.english: shall bear a son unto you, and you shall call his name Yitzchak ["He shall laugh"],

pairs.hebrew: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֥י אִתּ֛וֹ לִבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לְזַרְע֥וֹ אַחֲרָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and I shall establish My covenant [of circumcision] with him, [and not with the sons of Ishmael and Keturah], an everlasting covenant, for his seed after him.
And, as for Ishmael, I have heard you.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ בֵּרַ֣כְתִּי אֹת֗וֹ וְהִפְרֵיתִ֥י אֹת֛וֹ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֥י אֹת֖וֹ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: Behold, I have blessed him and have made him fruitful, and have multiplied him exceedingly.
Twelve princes (nesi'im) [also construable as "clouds" (which will vanish)] will he beget,
and I shall make him a great nation.
And My covenant shall I establish with Isaac [(Isaac was "holy", i.e., circumcised, from birth)],

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֩ תֵּלֵ֨ד לְךָ֤ שָׂרָה֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֣ד הַזֶּ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הָאַחֶֽרֶת׃
pairs.english: whom Sarah will bear unto you at this time in the following year.
And He finished speaking with him,
and G-d went up from Abraham, [(the righteous being the "chariot" of the L-rd)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בְּנ֗וֹ וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־יְלִידֵ֤י בֵיתוֹ֙ וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־מִקְנַ֣ת כַּסְפּ֔וֹ כׇּל־זָכָ֕ר בְּאַנְשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית אַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Abraham took Ishmael his son and all that were born in his house and all that were bought with his money, every male of the men of Abraham's household,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֜מׇל אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר עׇרְלָתָ֗ם בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin. On this very same day,

[in the daytime and not at night, (not fearing heathens or mockers, and (also) so that his foes and his contemporaries not say: Had we seen him, we would not have permitted him to do G-d's bidding)], as G-d had spoken to him.
And Abraham was ninety-nine years old
when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old
when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
On this very same day, [when Abraham had completed his ninety-ninth year, and Ishmael, his thirteenth,]
Abraham and Ishmael his son were circumcised.
And all the men of his house,
born in the house
or bought with money from a stranger,
were circumcised with him.
And the L-rd appeared to him [to "visit the sick," it being the third day after his circumcision,]
in the terebinths of Mamre, [Mamre having counseled him concerning circumcision].
And he sat at the opening of the tent [to host passersby]
in the heat of the day.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים
pairs.english: And he lifted his eyes and he saw, and, behold, three men [i.e., angels]
were standing over him, [one to give tidings to Sarah (that she would bear a son), one to overturn Sodom, and one to heal Abraham.]
And he saw [that they were hesitating to approach him], and he ran towards them from the opening of the tent,
and he bowed down to the ground.
And he said [to the greatest of them]:
My lord,
if I have now found favor in your eyes,
do not now pass away from your servant.
Let there be taken now a little water and wash your feet
[(Abraham taking them for Arabs, who bow down idolatrously "to the dust of their feet")],
and recline under the tree.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶקְחָ֨ה פַת־לֶ֜חֶם וְסַעֲד֤וּ לִבְּכֶם֙ אַחַ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֔רוּ
pairs.english: And I shall take a piece of bread, and feast your hearts, and then pass on.
For you have therefore passed by (the domicile of) your servant.
And they said: So do, as you have spoken.
And Abraham hurried to the tent, to Sarah,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת
pairs.english: and he said: Bring quickly three measures of meal [to cover the pot], fine flour [for cakes],
and knead it, and make cakes.
And Abraham ran to the herd,
and he took a calf, tender and good,
and he gave it to the youth [Ishmael],
and he hurried to dress it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן־הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And he took cream and milk and the calf which he had dressed, and he set it before them,
and he stood over them under the tree
and they [gave the impression that they] ate.
And they said to him: Where is Sarah, your wife?
And he said: Behold, she is in the tent. [(She is modest.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה
pairs.english: And he said: I [the L-rd] shall surely return to you at this time [Pesach] next year,
and, behold, a son to Sarah your wife.

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And Sarah was listening at the opening of the tent, and it [the opening] was behind him [the angel].
And Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in years.
There had ceased in Sarah the way of women [i.e., menstruation].
And Sarah laughed in [i.e., concerning] her innards, saying:
After withering, I have been rejuvenated,
and my lord is old.
And the L-rd said to Abraham:

pairs.hebrew: לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי׃
pairs.english: Why, now, did Sarah laugh, saying: "Will I in truth give birth when I am old?" [(Scripture alters her words here for "the sake of peace." She really said: "when my lord is old.")]
Is anything beyond the L-rd?

pairs.hebrew: לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן׃
pairs.english: At the appointed time I will return to you, at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.
And Sarah denied, saying: "I did not laugh," for she was afraid.
And He said: "No, but you did laugh!"

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ מִשָּׁם֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקִ֖פוּ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם
pairs.english: And the men arose from there, and they lowered at the face of Sodom.
And Abraham went with them to escort them.
And the L-rd said:

pairs.hebrew: הַֽמְכַסֶּ֤ה אֲנִי֙ מֵֽאַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה׃
pairs.english: Shall I conceal from Abraham what I am going to do [to Sodom]?

pairs.hebrew: וְאַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם הָי֧וֹ יִֽהְיֶ֛ה לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל וְעָצ֑וּם
pairs.english: — when Abraham is destined to be a great and mighty nation
in whom all the nations of the world will be blessed?

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י יְדַעְתִּ֗יו לְמַ֩עַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֶת־בָּנָ֤יו וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְשָֽׁמְרוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: For I have known him because he commands his children and his household after him to keep the way of the L-rd
to do righteousness and judgment

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֗עַן הָבִ֤יא יְהֹוָה֙ עַל־אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֖ר עָלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: so that the L-rd bring upon Abraham what He spoke concerning him.
And the L-rd said:

pairs.hebrew: זַעֲקַ֛ת סְדֹ֥ם וַעֲמֹרָ֖ה כִּי־רָ֑בָּה וְחַ֨טָּאתָ֔ם כִּ֥י כָבְדָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
pairs.english: The outcry of Sodom and Amorah, because it has become great, and their sin, because it is very heavy —
I shall go down now and I shall see:
If according to its outcry which comes unto Me, they have done [and persist in doing, I shall bring] destruction [upon them].
And if [they do] not [persist in their evil], I shall know [how to exact retribution for what they have already done].
And the men turned from there [whence Abraham had accompanied them], and they went to Sodom;
and Abraham still stood before the L-rd.
And Abraham drew near [to contend, to conciliate, and to pray], and he said:
Will You also cause to perish the righteous one with the wicked one?

pairs.hebrew: אוּלַ֥י יֵ֛שׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים צַדִּיקִ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר
pairs.english: Perhaps there are fifty righteous ones in the midst of the city, [ten for each district, there being five (distinct) places] —

pairs.hebrew: הַאַ֤ף תִּסְפֶּה֙ וְלֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א לַמָּק֔וֹם לְמַ֛עַן חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים הַצַּדִּיקִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃
pairs.english: Will You also cause to perish — and will You not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones in its midst?

pairs.hebrew: חָלִ֨לָה לְּךָ֜ מֵעֲשֹׂ֣ת ׀ כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה לְהָמִ֤ית צַדִּיק֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע
pairs.english: It is profane in You to do such a thing, to kill a righteous one with a wicked one,
rendering the righteous one like the wicked one.
It is profane in You.
Will the Judge of all the land not do justice?
And the L-rd said:

pairs.hebrew: אִם־אֶמְצָ֥א בִסְדֹ֛ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים צַדִּיקִ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר
pairs.english: If I find in Sodom fifty righteous ones in the midst of the city,
then I shall spare the entire place [i.e., all (five) districts] for their sake.
And Abraham answered and he said:
I have now willed to speak to the L-rd
when I should [already] have been [reduced to] dust [by the kings] and ashes [by Nimrod].
Perhaps there shall lack of the fifty righteous ones, five.
Will You destroy the entire city because of the five [and not add Yourself as a "righteous One" to each district to save the whole]?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִ֔ית אִם־אֶמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃
pairs.english: And He said: I shall not destroy if I find there forty-five.
And he ventured to speak more unto Him and he said:
Perhaps there will be found there forty [in four districts. Will You not save those districts?]
And He said: I shall not do [i.e., destroy] for the sake of the forty.
And he said: Let not the L-rd be wroth and I will speak.
Perhaps there will be found there thirty.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֔ה אִם־אֶמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם שְׁלֹשִֽׁים׃
pairs.english: And He said: I shall not do if I find there thirty.
And he said: Behold, I have willed to speak to the L-rd.
Perhaps there will be found there twenty.
And He said: I will not destroy for the sake of the twenty.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יֹּ֠אמֶר אַל־נָ֞א יִ֤חַר לַֽאדֹנָי֙ וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה אַךְ־הַפַּ֔עַם
pairs.english: And he said: Let not the L-rd be wroth and I will speak but this [last] time.
Perhaps there will be found there ten.

And He said: I will not destroy for the sake of the ten. [He did not venture to plead for less, reasoning from the fact that Noach, his sons, and their wives (eight altogether), had failed to save their generation (and having sought for but not having found nine in combination with the L-rd)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd went when He finished speaking with Abraham,
and Abraham returned to his place.
And the two angels, [one to destroy Sodom; the other, to save Lot,] came to Sodom in the evening.
And Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom [having that day been appointed as a judge.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא־לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קׇם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה׃
pairs.english: And Lot saw and he arose towards them, and he bowed down with his face to the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא־אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל־בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֙ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And he said: Behold, now, my lords: Turn, now, [by a side-path so that you not be noticed] to the house of your servant, and sleep over and wash your feet, [afterwards, so that the men of Sodom think you to be recently arrived, and not fault me for having hidden you from them],
and rise early and go on your way.
And they said: No, but we will sleep over in the street.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְצַר־בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ
pairs.english: And he greatly implored them, and they turned aside to him and they came to his house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
pairs.english: And he made a feast for them, and he baked matzoth, [it being Pesach], and they ate.

pairs.hebrew: טֶ֘רֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּ֒בוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל־הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד־זָקֵ֑ן
pairs.english: They had not yet lain down, when the people of the city, the people of Sodom [i.e., evildoers], surrounded the house, from young to old —
all of the people, from [one] end [of the city to the other (i.e., none protesting)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֶל־לוֹט֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ אַיֵּ֧ה הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַלָּ֑יְלָה
pairs.english: And they called to Lot and they said to him: Where are the men who came to you this night?
Bring them out to us that we may know [i.e., cohabit with] them.
And Lot went out to them at the door
and he closed the door behind him.
And he said:
Do not, I pray you, my brothers, do ill.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה־נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ
pairs.english: Behold, now, I have two daughters who have not known a man.

pairs.hebrew: אוֹצִֽיאָה־נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: Let me take them out now to you, and do to them as you wish.

pairs.hebrew: רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל־תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי׃
pairs.english: But to these men do not do anything; for therefore have they come under the shade of my roof.
And they said [in respect to his offering his daughters]: "Betake yourself."
And they said [in respect to his shielding of the angels]: The one [Lot] came to sojourn and he would be a judge!
Now we shall harm you more than them!

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְצְר֨וּ בָאִ֤ישׁ בְּלוֹט֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֖וּ לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר הַדָּֽלֶת׃
pairs.english: And they pressed upon the man, Lot, and they drew near to break down the door.
And the men sent forth their hands
and they brought Lot unto them into the house,
and they shut the door.

pairs.hebrew: וְֽאֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים אֲשֶׁר־פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֗יִת הִכּוּ֙ בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֔ים מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל
pairs.english: And the men at the entrance of the house they smote with blindness, from small, [who had initiated the transgression (19:4)], to great,
and they wearied themselves to find the entrance.
And the men said to Lot:
Who else [besides your wife and your daughters at home] do you have here?
[(If you have)] a son-in-law, or your sons [from your married daughters] and your daughters,
and all that you have in the city —
take it from the place.
For we are going to destroy this place.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־גָדְלָ֤ה צַעֲקָתָם֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥נוּ יְהֹוָ֖ה לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: For their outcry has grown great before the L-rd and the L-rd has sent us to destroy it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֨א ל֜וֹט וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר ׀ אֶל־חֲתָנָ֣יו ׀ לֹקְחֵ֣י בְנֹתָ֗יו
pairs.english: And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law [(He had two married daughters in the city)] [and to] the takers of his daughters [i.e., the men to whom his two daughters at home were betrothed],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִן־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־מַשְׁחִ֥ית יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶת־הָעִ֑יר
pairs.english: and he said: Arise, go out of this place; for the L-rd is going to destroy the city.
And he was as a jester in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
And when the morning star rose [see 24],
the angels rushed Lot, saying:

pairs.hebrew: קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת־אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת
pairs.english: Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found [at home],
lest you perish in the sin of the city.
And he lingered [to save his wealth],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּחֲזִ֨יקוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֣וֹ וּבְיַד־אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּבְיַד֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו בְּחֶמְלַ֥ת יְהֹוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו
pairs.english: and the men took hold of his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hand of his two daughters, in the L-rd's mercy upon him,
and they took him out, and they placed him outside the city.
And it was, when they took them outside, that he [the angel deputed to save Lot] said:
Escape with your life [and give no heed to your wealth].
Do not look behind you [at the destruction of Sodom, when you yourself are being saved.] And do not stand in the entire plain [of the Jordan].
Escape to the mountain [i.e., to Abraham, who dwells on the mountain (12:8)], lest you perish.
And Lot said to them:
Do not [urge me to escape to the mountain], I pray You, O L-rd —

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה־נָ֠א מָצָ֨א עַבְדְּךָ֣ חֵן֮ בְּעֵינֶ֒יךָ֒ וַתַּגְדֵּ֣ל חַסְדְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ עִמָּדִ֔י לְהַחֲי֖וֹת אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֑י
pairs.english: Behold, now, Your servant has found favor in Your eyes, and You have magnified Your lovingkindness which You did with me to keep my soul alive.

pairs.hebrew: וְאָנֹכִ֗י לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לְהִמָּלֵ֣ט הָהָ֔רָה פֶּן־תִּדְבָּקַ֥נִי הָרָעָ֖ה וָמַֽתִּי׃
pairs.english: I cannot escape to the mountain lest evil be imputed to me [relative to the righteousness of Abraham], and I die.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה־נָ֠א הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֧את קְרֹבָ֛ה לָנ֥וּס שָׁ֖מָּה וְהִ֣וא מִצְעָ֑ר
pairs.english: Behold, now, this city is close by to flee there, and it is small, [with few people, so that it may be spared].

pairs.hebrew: אִמָּלְטָ֨ה נָּ֜א שָׁ֗מָּה הֲלֹ֥א מִצְעָ֛ר הִ֖וא וּתְחִ֥י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
pairs.english: Let me escape there, I pray You — Is it not small? [so that it may be spared], and my soul will live.
And He said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה֙ נָשָׂ֣אתִי פָנֶ֔יךָ גַּ֖ם לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י הׇפְכִּ֥י אֶת־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃
pairs.english: I have granted you favor also for this thing [(that the entire city be saved for your sake)], not to overthrow the city of which you spoke.
Hurry, escape there.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת דָּבָ֔ר עַד־בֹּאֲךָ֖ שָׁ֑מָּה
pairs.english: For I shall not be able to do anything until you come there.
For this reason [i.e., that it is small (mitzar)], the city is called Tzoar.
The sun rose upon the earth
and Lot came to Tzoar.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֗ה הִמְטִ֧יר עַל־סְדֹ֛ם וְעַל־עֲמֹרָ֖ה גׇּפְרִ֣ית וָאֵ֑שׁ
pairs.english: And the L-rd [He and His beth-din] had rained down upon Sodom and Amorah [when the morning star had risen (15), (when both sun and moon were in the heavens, so that no opening be given to sun or moon worshippers to attribute the destruction to the absence of their deity) rain which changed to] brimstone and fire,
from the L-rd, from the heavens [the source of judgment].
And He overturned these cities [(the four were situated on one rock, which He overturned] and the entire plain,
and all the inhabitants of the cities, and the growth of the ground.
And his wife looked from [i.e., when she was] behind him,
and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham arose early in the morning
(to go) to the place where he had stood before the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף עַל־פְּנֵ֤י סְדֹם֙ וַעֲמֹרָ֔ה וְעַֽל־כׇּל־פְּנֵ֖י אֶ֣רֶץ הַכִּכָּ֑ר
pairs.english: And he looked out upon Sodom and Amorah and upon all the land of the plain,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה עָלָה֙ קִיטֹ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ כְּקִיטֹ֖ר הַכִּבְשָֽׁן׃
pairs.english: and he saw, and, behold, the smoke-column of the land rose as the smoke-column of a limekiln.
And it was, when G-d destroyed the cities of the plain,
that G-d remembered Abraham,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְשַׁלַּ֤ח אֶת־לוֹט֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָ֔ה בַּהֲפֹךְ֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יָשַׁ֥ב בָּהֵ֖ן לֽוֹט׃
pairs.english: and He sent Lot from the midst of the overturning, when He overturned the cities where Lot dwelt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֩עַל֩ ל֨וֹט מִצּ֜וֹעַר וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בָּהָ֗ר וּשְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: And Lot went up from Tzoar and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters with him,
for he was afraid to dwell in Tzoar, [it being too close to Sodom],
and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters.
And the elder said to the younger:
Our father is old [and "if not now, when?"],

pairs.hebrew: וְאִ֨ישׁ אֵ֤ין בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ לָב֣וֹא עָלֵ֔ינוּ כְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כׇּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and there is no man to cohabit with us in the way of all the land. [They assumed that all had perished as in the time of the flood.]

pairs.hebrew: לְכָ֨ה נַשְׁקֶ֧ה אֶת־אָבִ֛ינוּ יַ֖יִן וְנִשְׁכְּבָ֣ה עִמּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: Let us go and make our father drink wine and let us live with him
and let us bring our father's seed to life.
And they made their father drink wine that night [(Wine was "readied" for them in the cave for the bringing forth of two nations)].
And the elder came and lay with her father,
and he did not know in her lying and in her rising.
And it was on the morrow, that the elder said to the younger:
I lay yesterday with my father.

pairs.hebrew: נַשְׁקֶ֨נּוּ יַ֜יִן גַּם־הַלַּ֗יְלָה וּבֹ֙אִי֙ שִׁכְבִ֣י עִמּ֔וֹ וּנְחַיֶּ֥ה מֵאָבִ֖ינוּ זָֽרַע׃
pairs.english: Let us give him wine to drink this night, too; and come, lie with him, and we will bring our father's seed to life.

pairs.hebrew: וַתַּשְׁקֶ֜יןָ גַּ֣ם בַּלַּ֧יְלָה הַה֛וּא אֶת־אֲבִיהֶ֖ן יָ֑יִן
pairs.english: And they gave their father wine to drink on that night, too.
And the younger arose and lay with him.
And he did not know, in her lying down or in her getting up.
And the two daughters of Lot
conceived from their father.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֤לֶד הַבְּכִירָה֙ בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ מוֹאָ֑ב
pairs.english: And the elder bore a son, and she called him Moav (lit., "from the father").
He is the father of Moav until this day.
And the younger — she, too, bore a son,
and she called him Ben-Ami (lit., "son of my people").
He is the father of the sons of Ammon until this day.
And Abraham traveled from there to the land of the south, [seeing that wayfarers had ceased with the destruction of the cities].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בֵּין־קָדֵ֖שׁ וּבֵ֣ין שׁ֑וּר וַיָּ֖גׇר בִּגְרָֽר׃
pairs.english: And he dwelt between Kadesh and Shur, and he lived in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife:
"She is my sister."

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גְּרָ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־שָׂרָֽה׃
pairs.english: And Avimelech, the king of Gerar, sent and took Sarah.
And G-d came to Avimelech in a dream by night,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִנְּךָ֥ מֵת֙ עַל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־לָקַ֔חְתָּ
pairs.english: and He said: Behold, you shall die because of the woman you have taken,
for she is another man's wife.
And Avimelech did not come near to her, [an angel preventing him],
and he said:
Do You then slay even a righteous nation [(i.e., the generation of the flood and of Bavel) as You now threaten to slay me?]
Did he not say to me: "She is my sister"?
And she, also she, [(including her bondsmen, camel drivers, and ass drivers)] said to me: "He is my brother."
With innocence of heart, [not thinking to sin], and with cleanness of hands, [not having touched her] did I do this.
And G-d said to him in a dream:

pairs.hebrew: גַּ֣ם אָנֹכִ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ כִּ֤י בְתׇם־לְבָבְךָ֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּ֔את
pairs.english: I, too, know that you did this with innocence of heart, [not thinking to sin; but there is no "cleanness of hands" here,]
for I, too, kept you from sinning to Me,
wherefore I did not enable you to touch her.
And, now, return the man's wife, [and do not think he will not take her back, assuming that you have lived with her, or that he will hate you and not pray for you],
for he is a prophet [and he knows that you have not touched her], and he will pray for you, and you will live.

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־אֵֽינְךָ֣ מֵשִׁ֔יב דַּ֚ע כִּי־מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת אַתָּ֖ה וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And if you do not return (her), know that you will surely die, you and all that is yours.
And Avimelech arose early in the morning and he called all of his servants
and he spoke all of these words in their ears,
and the men feared greatly.
And Avimelech called to Abraham and said to him:

pairs.hebrew: מֶֽה־עָשִׂ֤יתָ לָּ֙נוּ֙ וּמֶֽה־חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־הֵבֵ֧אתָ עָלַ֛י וְעַל־מַמְלַכְתִּ֖י חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה
pairs.english: What did you do to us and how have I sinned to you that you have brought upon me and my kingdom a great sin?
Things that are not done have you done with me, [i.e., You have brought upon us an unnatural plague, the stoppage of all natural passages].
And Avimelech said to Abraham:

pairs.hebrew: מָ֣ה רָאִ֔יתָ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: What did you see that you did this thing?
And Abraham said:

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי רַ֚ק אֵין־יִרְאַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: For I said: There is surely no fear of G-d in this place [When one comes to a city should they ask him whether he is in need of lodging or whether the woman with him is his wife or his sister!],
and they will slay me because of my wife.

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם־אׇמְנָ֗ה אֲחֹתִ֤י בַת־אָבִי֙ הִ֔וא אַ֖ךְ לֹ֣א בַת־אִמִּ֑י
pairs.english: And also, in truth, she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother,
and she became my wife. [(Sarah, the daughter of Abraham's brother Haran (11:29) is considered the daughter of his father, and a sister by one's father is permitted to a Noachide.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְע֣וּ אֹתִ֗י אֱלֹהִים֮ מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֒
pairs.english: And it was, when G-d caused me to wander from my father's house,

pairs.hebrew: וָאֹמַ֣ר לָ֔הּ זֶ֣ה חַסְדֵּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשִׂ֖י עִמָּדִ֑י
pairs.english: I said to her, [realizing that we would pass through places of evildoers]: This is your lovingkindness that you shall do with me:

pairs.hebrew: אֶ֤ל כׇּל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה אִמְרִי־לִ֖י אָחִ֥י הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: Wherever we come, say about me: "He is my brother."

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֗ר וַעֲבָדִים֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְאַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Avimelech took flocks and herds and bondsmen and bondswomen and he gave them to Abraham [to conciliate him so that he would pray for him],
and he returned to him Sarah his wife.
And Avimelech said:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֥ה אַרְצִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ בַּטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ שֵֽׁב׃
pairs.english: Here is my land before you; dwell wherever you like.

pairs.hebrew: וּלְשָׂרָ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֜תִּי אֶ֤לֶף כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לְאָחִ֔יךְ
pairs.english: And to Sarah he said [in conciliation]: Behold, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your brother.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה הוּא־לָךְ֙ כְּס֣וּת עֵינַ֔יִם לְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: It is a "covering of the eyes" for you of all who are with you, [that they not look lightly upon you, assuming you to have been violated by me and then discarded, (the payment indicating that I was "forced" to give you up)],
and (it is a covering of the eyes) of all [men] and proof [that you have not been violated].
And Abraham prayed to G-d,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְפָּ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֧לֶךְ וְאֶת־אִשְׁתּ֛וֹ וְאַמְהֹתָ֖יו וַיֵּלֵֽדוּ׃
pairs.english: and G-d healed Avimelech and his wife and his bondswomen, and they were relieved [i.e., their passages were opened].

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־עָצֹ֤ר עָצַר֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד כׇּל־רֶ֖חֶם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ
pairs.english: For the L-rd had stopped up every passage in the house of Avimelech
at the bidding of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
And the L-rd had visited Sarah [even before healing Avimelech, (one who prays for his neighbor — as Abraham did for Avimelech — being answered first)], as He had said [regarding conception (17:19)],
and the L-rd did unto Sarah as He had spoken [to Abraham regarding the birth of an heir (15:1)].

pairs.hebrew: וַתַּ֩הַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age,
at the appointed time of which G-d had spoken [18:4].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת־שֶׁם־בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד־ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה־לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה
pairs.english: And Abraham called the name of the son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore unto him,
Isaac.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤מׇל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son when he was eight days old,
as G-d had commanded him.
And Abraham was a hundred years old
when Isaac his son was born to him.
And Sarah said:
G-d made rejoicing for me.
All who hear will rejoice for me.
And she said: Who is it [(i.e., see how exalted He is)] who said [(milel, 100 in gematria) that in the hundredth year]
of Abraham Sarah would suckle children [(the matrons bringing their children to her to be nursed)],
for I have borne a son in his old age.
And the child grew and he was weaned [after twenty-four months],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃
pairs.english: and Abraham made a great feast [i.e., one attended by the great men of the generation] on the day that Isaac was weaned.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶֽת־בֶּן־הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם
pairs.english: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham,
disporting himself [with idolatry].

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת־בְּנָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And she said to Abraham: Drive out this maidservant and her son.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן־הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם־בְּנִ֖י עִם־יִצְחָֽק׃
pairs.english: For the son of this maidservant will not inherit with my son [(even if he were not Isaac)], with Isaac [(even if he were not my son)].
And the thing was very bad in the eyes of Abraham
because of [being asked to drive out] his son.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֗ם אַל־יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ עַל־הַנַּ֣עַר וְעַל־אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And G-d said to Abraham: Let it not be bad in your eyes because of the youth and because of your maidservant.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֛יךָ שָׂרָ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלָ֑הּ
pairs.english: Whatever Sarah says to you, hearken to her [(whence we derive that Abraham was secondary to Sarah in prophecy)];
for in Isaac will there be called seed unto you.
And also the son of the maidservant I shall make a nation of him,
for he is your seed.
And Abraham rose early in the morning
and he took bread and a skin-vessel of water, [but not silver and gold, for he hated Ishmael for having become corrupt],
and he gave it to Hagar, placing it on her shoulder, along with the child [(Sarah having cast an evil eye upon him, rendering him feverish and unable to walk)],
and he sent her and she went;
and she strayed [She returned to the idolatry of her father's house] in the desert of Beersheva.
And the water in the skin-vessel was finished
and she cast the child under one of the growths.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֩לֶךְ֩ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב לָ֜הּ מִנֶּ֗גֶד הַרְחֵק֙ כִּמְטַחֲוֵ֣י קֶ֔שֶׁת
pairs.english: And she went and she sat from afar, about two bow shots away.
For she said: Let me not see the death of the child.
And [when he was close to death], she sat down farther off, and she lifted up her voice and she cried.
And G-d heard the voice of the youth [(whence it is derived that the sick one's plaint is sooner heard and answered than the prayer of others for him)],
and an angel of G-d called to Hagar from heaven,
and he said to her: What grieves you, Hagar?
Do not fear.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא־שָֽׁם׃
pairs.english: For G-d has heard the voice of the child in his present station. [For the ministering angels protested Ishmael's being saved from thirst when he was destined to cause Israel to die of thirst (see Isaiah 21:13-14), and G-d answered that he was being judged according to his present (guiltless) status].

pairs.hebrew: ק֚וּמִי שְׂאִ֣י אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר וְהַחֲזִ֥יקִי אֶת־יָדֵ֖ךְ בּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: Arise, lift up the child and strengthen your hand in him,
for I shall make him a great nation.
And G-d opened her eyes
and she beheld a well of water,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּ֤א אֶת־הַחֵ֙מֶת֙ מַ֔יִם וַתַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־הַנָּֽעַר׃
pairs.english: and she went and filled up the skin-vessel with water, and she gave the youth to drink.
And G-d was with the youth, and he grew up,
and he dwelt in the desert and became a bowman.
And he dwelt in the desert of Paran,
and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Egypt [where she had been reared.]

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And it was at that time that Avimelech and Phichol, the captain of his host, [seeing that Abraham had escaped the destruction of the region of Sodom, that he had defeated the kings (section 14), and that his wife had borne a child to him in his old age] said to Abraham:
G-d is with you in all that you do.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֨בְעָה לִּ֤י בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה אִם־תִּשְׁקֹ֣ר לִ֔י וּלְנִינִ֖י וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י
pairs.english: And, now, swear to me here by G-d that you will not deal falsely with me, or with my child, or with my grandchild, [(thus far, a man's compassion for his children)].

pairs.hebrew: כַּחֶ֜סֶד אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֤יתִי עִמְּךָ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עִמָּדִ֔י וְעִם־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־גַּ֥רְתָּה בָּֽהּ׃
pairs.english: As the lovingkindness that I did with you [viz. (20:15): "Behold, my land is before you"] do with me and with the land in which you dwelt.
And Abraham said:
I shall swear.
And Abraham contended with Avimelech

pairs.hebrew: עַל־אֹדוֹת֙ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּזְל֖וּ עַבְדֵ֥י אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
pairs.english: over the well of water that the servants of Avimelech had stolen.
And Avimelech said:

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: I do not know who did this thing,
and you, too, did not tell me,

pairs.hebrew: וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בִּלְתִּ֥י הַיּֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: and I, too, did not hear of it until today.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ
pairs.english: And Abraham took sheep and kine and gave them to Avimelech
and the two of them made a covenant.
And Abraham stood the seven ewe-lambs of the flock
by themselves.
And Avimelech said to Abraham:

pairs.hebrew: מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה שֶׁ֤בַע כְּבָשֹׂת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצַּ֖בְתָּ לְבַדָּֽנָה׃
pairs.english: What are these seven ewe-lambs which you have stood by themselves?
And he said:
For seven ewe-lambs shall you take from my hand,
that this [the waters of the well miraculously rising to Abraham in "confirmation" of his ownership] be a testimony unto me
that I have dug this well.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע
pairs.english: Therefore, he called that place Beersheva,
for there they both swore (nishbe'u).
And they made a covenant in Beersheva,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣קׇם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
pairs.english: and Avimelech arose, and Phichol, the captain of his host, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
And he planted a fruit grove in Beersheva,

and he called there in the name of the L-rd, the G-d of the world. [As a result of that fruit grove the L-rd came to be called the G-d of the whole world, Abraham charging his guests to bless the Creator of the whole world, whose fruits they had eaten.]
And Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines
many days [(twenty-six years, one year more than he had lived in Chevron)].
And it was, after these things,
that G-d proved Abraham.
He said to him: "Abraham,"
and he said: "Here I am" [ready to do Your bidding].
And He said:
Take, I pray you, [(Stand firm for Me in this trial)]
your son [(Abraham: I have two sons)],
your only one [(Abraham: Each is the only one of his mother)],
whom you love [(Abraham: I love them both)] —
Isaac [(All this, so as not to overwhelm Abraham by springing the command upon him, and, also, to endear the mitzvah to him)],
and go to the land of Moriah [Jerusalem],
and bring him up there as a burnt-offering

pairs.hebrew: עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: on one of the mountains that I shall indicate to you.
And Abraham arose early in the morning [in haste to perform the mitzvah], and he [himself] saddled his ass,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י נְעָרָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑וֹ
pairs.english: and he took his two youths [Ishmael and Eliezer] with him, and Isaac his son;

pairs.hebrew: וַיְבַקַּע֙ עֲצֵ֣י עֹלָ֔ה וַיָּ֣קׇם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אָֽמַר־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
pairs.english: and he split wood for the burnt-offering, and he arose, and he went to the place which G-d had designated to him.

On the third day, [(Abraham not being shown the place immediately so that it not be said that he was "stunned" into the sacrifice and that if he had had time to deliberate he would not have undertaken it)],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֧ם אֶת־עֵינָ֛יו וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־הַמָּק֖וֹם מֵרָחֹֽק׃
pairs.english: Abraham lifted his eyes, and he saw the place from afar, [a cloud hovering over the mountain.]
And Abraham said to his youths:
Abide here with the ass

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֣י וְהַנַּ֔עַר נֵלְכָ֖ה עַד־כֹּ֑ה וְנִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and I and the youth will go [a little way off] to this [place before us], and we will prostrate ourselves and we will return to you [(Abraham prophesying that they would return)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֙שֶׂם֙ עַל־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ
pairs.english: And Abraham took the wood for the burnt-offering and placed it upon Isaac his son.
And he took in his hand the kindling and the knife,
and both went together [i.e., in the same spirit — Abraham, who knew, as happy as Isaac, who did not know].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to Abraham his father: And he said: "My father."
And he said: "Here I am, my son."

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה׃
pairs.english: And he said: "Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt-offering?"
And Abraham said:
G-d will see to the lamb for the burnt-offering, [and if there is no lamb, then it will be] my son.
And both went together [in the same spirit of happiness — even Isaac, who now knew that he was going to be slaughtered.]
And they came to the place which G-d had indicated to him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־הָעֵצִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Abraham built the altar there and he arranged the wood.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים׃
pairs.english: And he bound Isaac his son, [hands and feet tied behind him], and he placed him on the altar upon the wood.
And Abraham sent forth his hand
and he took the knife to slaughter his son.
And an angel of the L-rd called to him from heaven,
saying: "Abraham, Abraham" [(the doubling connoting affection)].
And he said: "Here I am."

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל־תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָה
pairs.english: And He said: Do not stretch your hand forth to the youth, and do not do anything to him.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת־בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת־יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
pairs.english: For now I know [i.e., I can counter all objections to My election of you; for it is evident to all] that you are G-d-fearing, not having spared your only son from Me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּה־אַ֔יִל אַחַ֕ר נֶאֱחַ֥ז בַּסְּבַ֖ךְ בְּקַרְנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Abraham lifted his eyes and he saw, and, behold, a ram afterwards, [i.e., after the angel had said to him: "Do not stretch, etc."] caught in the thicket by its horns.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אַבְרָהָם֙ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָאַ֔יִל וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ לְעֹלָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And Abraham went and he took the ram and brought it up as a burnt-offering in place of his son [i.e., For each sacrificial act, he prayed: "May it be Your will to reckon it as if it were done to my son."]
And Abraham called the name of that place "The L-rd will see" [i.e., He will choose for Himself that place for the reposing of His Shechinah and the sacrifice of offerings],

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה׃
pairs.english: of which [place] it will be said [in future generations]: "On this day in the mountain, the L-rd shall appear."
And an angel of the L-rd called to Abraham
a second time from heaven.
And he said: I have sworn by My name, says the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֖כְתָּ אֶת־בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת־יְחִידֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: that because you have done this thing and not spared your son, your only one,

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־בָרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֶכְךָ֗ וְהַרְבָּ֨ה אַרְבֶּ֤ה אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכַח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־שְׂפַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ם
pairs.english: that bless shall I bless you [(one blessing for the father, one for the son)] and multiply will I multiply your seed [(one for the father, one for the son)], as the stars of the heavens and the sand on the seashore,
and your seed shall inherit the gate of his foes.
And there will bless themselves in your seed all the nations of the earth,
because you have hearkened to My voice.
And Abraham returned to his youths
and they arose and went together to Beersheva,
and Abraham sojourned in Beersheva [(on the way to Chevron)].
And it was after these things [(i.e., after Abraham's thoughts on the binding of Isaac, viz.: If he had been slaughtered, he would have died without children — I should have gotten him a wife)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִ֠נֵּ֠ה יָלְדָ֨ה מִלְכָּ֥ה גַם־הִ֛וא בָּנִ֖ים לְנָח֥וֹר אָחִֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: that it was told to Abraham: Milkah, she, too, has borne sons to Nachor your brother [i.e., Her family, too, is similar to that of Abraham. Just as twelve tribes issued from Abraham by way of Jacob — eight from the principal wives and four from the concubines — here, too, there were eight sons from the principal wife and four from the concubine.]
Utz, his firstborn
and Buz, his brother, and Kemuel, the father of Aram.
And Kessed and Chazzo
and Pildash and Yidlaf
and Bethuel.
And Bethuel begot Rivkah [(The entire genealogy was recorded for the sake of this verse)].

pairs.hebrew: שְׁמֹנָ֥ה אֵ֙לֶּה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה מִלְכָּ֔ה לְנָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: These eight were borne by Milkah to Nachor the brother of Abraham.
And his concubine, whose name was Reumah,
she, too, bore:
Tevach and Gacham and Tachash and Ma'achah.
And the life of Sarah was

pairs.hebrew: מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֛ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים
pairs.english: a hundred years and twenty years [(Just as she had not sinned by twenty, sin liability not obtaining until that age, so she had not sinned by one hundred)], and seven years [(She was as beautiful at twenty as she was at seven)],
the years of the life of Sarah [All were uniform in goodness.]
And Sarah died

in Kiryath Arbah [("the city of the four" — so called either because of the four giants who lived there, or because of the four pairs who are buried there — Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rivkah, Jacob and Leah)], which is Chevron,
in the land of Canaan.
And Abraham came
[from Beersheva] to eulogize Sarah and to bewail her.
And Abraham arose from before his dead one,
and he spoke to the sons of Cheth, saying:
A stranger [from a different land] and a dweller am I with you.
Give me a (land) holding for a burial plot with you
so that I may bury my dead one from before me.
And the sons of Cheth answered Abraham,
saying to him:
Hear us, my lord,
you are a prince of G-d in our midst.
In the choicest of our plots bury your dead one;

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אֶת־קִבְר֛וֹ לֹֽא־יִכְלֶ֥ה מִמְּךָ֖ מִקְּבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: none of us will hold back his plot from you from burying your dead one.
And Abraham arose
and he prostrated himself to the people of the land, to the sons of Cheth.
And he spoke to them, saying:
If it is your will to bury my dead one from before me,
hear me and petition Efron the son of Tzochar for me.
And let him give me the doubled cave [(so called because it had an upper and a lower story or because it was "doubled with pairs")], which he has,
which is at the end of his field.

pairs.hebrew: בְּכֶ֨סֶף מָלֵ֜א יִתְּנֶ֥נָּה לִּ֛י בְּתוֹכְכֶ֖ם לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃
pairs.english: For its full value let him give it (i.e., sell it) to me, in your midst as holding for a burial plot.
And Efron was sitting in the midst of the sons of Cheth, [having that day been appointed an officer in consideration of Abraham's being beholden to him].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֩עַן֩ עֶפְר֨וֹן הַחִתִּ֤י אֶת־אַבְרָהָם֙ בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֔ת
pairs.english: And Efron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Cheth,
for all who had come to the gate of his city [(All had left their work to come to pay respect to Sarah)],
saying:
No, my lord, [do not pay for it], hear me.
The field — I have given it to you;
and the cave that is in it, to you have I given it.
Before the eyes of the sons of my people have I given it to you —
bury your dead one.
And Abraham prostrated himself
before the people of the land.
And he spoke to Efron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying:
But if you would only hear me.
I have set aside the money for the field — take it from me
and let me bury my dead one there.
And Efron answered Abraham,
saying to him:
My lord, hear me.

pairs.hebrew: אֶ֩רֶץ֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵאֹ֧ת שֶֽׁקֶל־כֶּ֛סֶף בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵֽינְךָ֖ מַה־הִ֑וא
pairs.english: Land worth four hundred shekels of silver, between [lovers like] you and me, what is it?
[Forget about it] and bury your dead one.
And Abraham hearkened to Efron,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ל אַבְרָהָם֙ לְעֶפְרֹ֔ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֕סֶף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֑ת
pairs.english: and Abraham weighed out to Efron the silver whereof he had spoken in the ears of the sons of Cheth,

pairs.hebrew: אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שֶׁ֣קֶל כֶּ֔סֶף עֹבֵ֖ר לַסֹּחֵֽר׃
pairs.english: four hundred shekels of silver, current with the merchant.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣קׇם ׀ שְׂדֵ֣ה עֶפְר֗וֹן אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּמַּכְפֵּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י מַמְרֵ֑א
pairs.english: And the field of Efron which was in the Machpelah before Mamre —

pairs.hebrew: הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְהַמְּעָרָ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔וֹ וְכׇל־הָעֵץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכׇל־גְּבֻל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
pairs.english: the field and the cave therein and all the trees in the field in all its boundaries roundabout — was confirmed
to Abraham as an acquisition
before the eyes of the sons of Cheth, before all who entered the gate of his city.
And after that, Abraham buried Sarah, his wife,

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־מְעָרַ֞ת שְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵ֖א הִ֣וא חֶבְר֑וֹן בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
pairs.english: in the cave of the field of the Machpelah, before Mamre, which is Chevron in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the cave therein were confirmed
to Abraham as a burial holding
from the sons of Cheth.
And Abraham was old, "come into the days,"
and the L-rd had blessed Abraham with everything [bakol, the gematria of ben (a son) — whence the need to find a wife for him].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶל־עַבְדּוֹ֙ זְקַ֣ן בֵּית֔וֹ הַמֹּשֵׁ֖ל בְּכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Abraham said to his bondsman, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that was his.

Place your hand beneath my thigh. [One who takes an oath must hold a sacred object in his hand. Circumcision, being Abraham's first mitzvah, and having been attended by pain, and being beloved by him, Abraham bade him take hold there.]

pairs.hebrew: וְאַשְׁבִּ֣יעֲךָ֔ בַּֽיהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And I will beswear you by the L-rd, the G-d of the heavens and the G-d of the earth,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: that you not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaani, in whose midst I dwell.
But to my land and to my birthplace shall you go,
and you shall take a wife for my son Isaac.
And the bondsman said to him:

pairs.hebrew: אוּלַי֙ לֹא־תֹאבֶ֣ה הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה לָלֶ֥כֶת אַחֲרַ֖י אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את
pairs.english: Perchance the woman will not want to go after me to this land.
Shall I return your son
to the land whence you came?
And Abraham said to him:
Take heed unto yourself lest you return my son there.

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לְקָחַ֜נִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֽוֹלַדְתִּי֒ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּר־לִ֜י וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע־לִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַ֨רְעֲךָ֔ אֶתֵּ֖ן אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את
pairs.english: The L-rd, the G-d of the heavens [(whereas above [3] we have: "the G-d of the heavens and the G-d of the earth," Abraham having taught men to regard Him as such)], who took me out of my father's house [Charan] and from the land of my birth [Ur Kasdim], and who spoke concerning me [i.e., in my behalf] and who swore to me [at the covenant between the pieces (15:18)]: "To your children will I give this land"] —

pairs.hebrew: ה֗וּא יִשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכוֹ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֛ה לִבְנִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃
pairs.english: He shall send his angel before you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman does not want to go after you,
then you will be clean of this oath of mine [and take a wife for him from the daughters of Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre];
only my son do not return there. [But Jacob, the son of my son, is destined to return there.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם הָעֶ֙בֶד֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ תַּ֛חַת יֶ֥רֶךְ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And the bondsman placed his hand under the thigh of Abraham, his master,
and he swore to him concerning this thing.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הָ֠עֶ֠בֶד עֲשָׂרָ֨ה גְמַלִּ֜ים מִגְּמַלֵּ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙
pairs.english: And the bondsman took ten camels of his master's camels, [distinctively his master's in being muzzled against grazing in the fields of others],
and he went, and all of the good of his master in his hand, [i.e., a deed of gift to Isaac of all that he owned, so that they "jump" at sending their daughter].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֗קׇם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־אֲרַ֥ם נַֽהֲרַ֖יִם אֶל־עִ֥יר נָחֽוֹר׃
pairs.english: And he arose and he went to Aram Naharayim [lit., "Aram of the two rivers," it being situated between two rivers], to the city of Nachor.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּבְרֵ֧ךְ הַגְּמַלִּ֛ים מִח֥וּץ לָעִ֖יר אֶל־בְּאֵ֣ר הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And he made his camels kneel outside the city by a well of water
towards evening, at the time that the (women) water-drawers go out.
And he said: O L-rd, G-d of my master, Abraham;

pairs.hebrew: הַקְרֵה־נָ֥א לְפָנַ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וַעֲשֵׂה־חֶ֕סֶד עִ֖ם אֲדֹנִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: make it chance, I pray you, before me today, and do lovingkindness with my master, Abraham.
Behold, I stand by the well of water,

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנוֹת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר יֹצְאֹ֖ת לִשְׁאֹ֥ב מָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and the daughters of the men of the city go out to draw water.
And the maiden to whom I shall say:
"Incline, I pray you, your pitcher, that I may drink,"
and who shall answer: "Drink, and your camels, too, shall I give to drink" —
her have You chosen for Your servant Isaac,
and, let me know, [I pray You], through her, [by her being of his family and fit for him],
that You have done lovingkindness with my master.
And it was, before he had finished speaking,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֧ה רִבְקָ֣ה יֹצֵ֗את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֻלְּדָה֙ לִבְתוּאֵ֣ל בֶּן־מִלְכָּ֔ה אֵ֥שֶׁת נָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: and, behold, Rivkah came out, who had been born to Bethuel the son of Milkah, the wife of Nachor, Abraham's brother,
with her pitcher on her shoulder.
And the maiden was very beautiful,
a virgin, and no man had known her [pederastically],
and she went down to the well,
and she filled up her pitcher,
and she went up.
And the bondsman ran towards her, [having seen the waters rising towards her],
and he said: Let me sip, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher.
And she said: "Drink, my lord."
And she hastened and she brought down her pitcher [from her shoulder] upon her hand, and she gave him to drink.
And she finished giving him to drink,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֤ם לִגְמַלֶּ֙יךָ֙ אֶשְׁאָ֔ב עַ֥ד אִם־כִּלּ֖וּ לִשְׁתֹּֽת׃
pairs.english: and she said: Also for your camels shall I draw, until they have finished drinking.
And she hastened, and she poured out her pitcher into the trough,
and she ran again to the well to draw water,
and she drew for all of his camels.
And the man looked in wonderment at her,
keeping silent to know
whether the L-rd had prospered his way [by her being of Abraham's family]
or not.
And it was, when the camels had finished drinking,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֤ח הָאִישׁ֙ נֶ֣זֶם זָהָ֔ב בֶּ֖קַע מִשְׁקָל֑וֹ
pairs.english: that the man took a golden nose ring, a beka in weight [(intimating the shekels of Israel, "a beka (half-shekel) for a head" (Exodus 28:36)],

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵ֤י צְמִידִים֙ עַל־יָדֶ֔יהָ עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מִשְׁקָלָֽם׃
pairs.english: and (placed) two clasps on her hands [(intimating the two "clasped" tablets of the Law)], ten (shekels of) gold their weight [(intimating the Ten Commandments)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בַּת־מִ֣י אַ֔תְּ הַגִּ֥ידִי נָ֖א לִ֑י
pairs.english: And he said: Whose daughter are you? Tell me, I pray you.
Is there place for us in your father's house for a night's lodging?
And she said to him, [answering first things first]: I am the daughter of Bethuel,
the son of Milkah, whom she bore to Nachor.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו גַּם־תֶּ֥בֶן גַּם־מִסְפּ֖וֹא רַ֣ב עִמָּ֑נוּ
pairs.english: And she said to him: Both straw and provender [(camel feed)] are abundant with us,
also a place for [many nights] lodgings.
And the man bowed down
and he prostrated himself to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲ֠שֶׁ֠ר לֹֽא־עָזַ֥ב חַסְדּ֛וֹ וַאֲמִתּ֖וֹ מֵעִ֣ם אֲדֹנִ֑י
pairs.english: And he said: Blessed is the L-rd, the G-d of my master Abraham, who did not leave off His lovingkindness and His truth from my master.

pairs.hebrew: אָנֹכִ֗י בַּדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ נָחַ֣נִי יְהֹוָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אֲחֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃
pairs.english: I, in the way [that I required], the L-rd has guided me, to the house of my master's brethren.
And the maiden ran
and she told of these things in her mother's house.
And Rivkah had a brother, and his name was Lavan,
and Lavan ran to the man outside, to the well.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כִּרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־הַנֶּ֗זֶם וְֽאֶת־הַצְּמִדִים֮ עַל־יְדֵ֣י אֲחֹתוֹ֒ וּכְשׇׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֞י רִבְקָ֤ה אֲחֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־דִבֶּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י הָאִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: And it was, when he saw the nose ring and the clasps on his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rivkah his sister: "Thus spoke the man to me" [that he ran, etc.],

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־הָאִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים עַל־הָעָֽיִן׃
pairs.english: and he came to the man, and, behold, he was standing over the camels [to watch them] at the well.
And he said: Come, blessed of the L-rd.
Why do you stand outside?
I have cleaned the house [of idolatry]
and (made) a place for the camels.
And the man came into the house and he unmuzzled the camels,
and he gave straw and provender to the camels,

pairs.hebrew: וּמַ֙יִם֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ רַגְלָ֔יו וְרַגְלֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
And food was placed before him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל עַ֥ד אִם־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי דְּבָרָ֑י
pairs.english: and he said: "I shall not eat until I have spoken my words."
And he said: "Speak."
And he said:
I am the bondsman of Abraham.
And the L-rd blessed my master greatly, and he prospered.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֶּן־ל֞וֹ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וַעֲבָדִם֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
pairs.english: And He gave him flocks and herds, and silver and gold, and bondsmen and bondswomen, and camels and asses.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֡לֶד שָׂרָה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת אֲדֹנִ֥י בֵן֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י זִקְנָתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And Sarah, the wife of my master, bore a son to my master after she had become old,
and he gave him all that was his. [He showed him the deed of gift.]
And my master beswore me, saying:

pairs.hebrew: לֹא־תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaani, in whose land I dwell.
Unless you go [first] to my father's house and to my family [and she refuse to go with you],
and you shall take a wife for my son.
And I said to my master:
Perchance the woman will not want to go after me.
And he said to me:

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנָ֗יו יִשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכ֤וֹ אִתָּךְ֙ וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֶּ֔ךָ
pairs.english: The L-rd, before whom I have walked, He will send His angel with you and He will prosper your way,
and you shall take a wife for my son
from my family and from my father's house.
Then you will be clean of my oath —
when you come to my family.
And if they do not give (her) to you,
you will be clean of my oath.
And I came this day [that I started out], to the well, [G-d having "shrunk the way" for me],
and I said; O L-rd, G-d of my master Abraham —
If You now prosper my way
upon which I go,
Behold, I stand by the well of water,

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֤ה הָֽעַלְמָה֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣את לִשְׁאֹ֔ב וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֵלֶ֔יהָ הַשְׁקִֽינִי־נָ֥א מְעַט־מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: and, the maiden who goes out to draw, and I say to her: "Give me to drink, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher,"
and she will say to me:
"You, too, [including the men who are with you] drink, and also for your camels will I draw" —
she is the woman
whom the L-rd has chosen for my master's son.
I, before I had finished speaking in my heart,
behold, Rivkah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יְנָה וַתִּשְׁאָ֑ב וָאֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ הַשְׁקִ֥ינִי נָֽא׃
pairs.english: and she went down to the well and she drew; and I said to her: "Give me to drink, I pray you."
And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder,
and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels to drink also:
so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
And I asked her: "Whose daughter are you?"

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ בֶּן־נָח֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽלְדָה־לּ֖וֹ מִלְכָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And she said: "The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nachor, whom Milkah bore to him."
