And I placed the ring on her nose and the clasps on her hands. [He changed the true order (placing-asking, 24:22-23), so that he not be "interrogated" on how he could have given before knowing who she was.]
And I bowed down and I prostrated myself to the L-rd,
and I blessed the L-rd, the G-d of my master, Abraham,
who led me in the way of truth,
to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠עַתָּ֠ה אִם־יֶשְׁכֶ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים חֶ֧סֶד וֶֽאֱמֶ֛ת אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֑י
pairs.english: And now, if you would do lovingkindness and truth with my master, tell me;
and if not, tell me.
And I will turn to the right [to the daughters of Ishmael] or to the left [to the daughters of Lot].
And Lavan and Bethuel answered. [Lavan, the wicked one, "jumping" to answer before his father]:
From the L-rd has the thing gone forth.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רַ֥ע אוֹ־טֽוֹב׃
pairs.english: We cannot speak to you [in refusal] ill or good.
Behold, Rivkah is before you, take (her) and go;

pairs.hebrew: וּתְהִ֤י אִשָּׁה֙ לְבֶן־אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: and let her be a wife to your master's son, as the L-rd has spoken.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֛ע עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And it was, when Abraham's bondsman heard their words,
that he bowed to the ground to the L-rd, [acknowledging good tidings].

pairs.hebrew: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א הָעֶ֜בֶד כְּלֵי־כֶ֨סֶף וּכְלֵ֤י זָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְרִבְקָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the bondsman took out vessels of silver and vessels of gold and garments, and he gave them to Rivkah;
and select fruits [from Eretz Yisrael] he gave to her brother and to her mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֗וּ ה֛וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֖וֹ וַיָּלִ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they stayed overnight,
and they arose in the morning; and he said: Send me to my master.
And her brother and her mother [(Bethuel, who wanted to renege, having been killed by an angel)] said:

pairs.hebrew: תֵּשֵׁ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֥ אִתָּ֛נוּ יָמִ֖ים א֣וֹ עָשׂ֑וֹר אַחַ֖ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃
pairs.english: Let the maiden remain with us a year or ten months; after that, let her go.
And he said to them: Do not delay me
when the L-rd has prospered my way.
Send me and let me go to my master.
And they said: Let us call the maiden
and ask her [if she consents].
And they called Rivkah and they said to her:
Will you go with this man?
And she said: I shall go, [even against your will].
And they sent Rivkah their sister and her nurse,
and Abraham's bondsman and his men.
And they blessed Rivkah and they said to her:
Our sister, may you [and not another woman be destined to receive the blessing given to Abraham on Mount Moriah (22:17). May you] become thousands of myriads,
and may your seed inherit the gate of its foes [Ibid.]

pairs.hebrew: וַתָּ֨קׇם רִבְקָ֜ה וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ וַתִּרְכַּ֙בְנָה֙ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וַתֵּלַ֖כְנָה אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: And Rivka and her maidens arose and they rode on the camels and they went after the man.
And the bondsman took Rivkah and he went.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִצְחָק֙ בָּ֣א מִבּ֔וֹא בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac had just come from Be'er Lachai Ro'i [(16:14) having gone there to bring Hagar back to Abraham as a wife],
and he dwelt in the land of the south.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק לָשׂ֥וּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת עָ֑רֶב
pairs.english: And Isaac went to pray in the field towards evening,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה גְמַלִּ֖ים בָּאִֽים׃
pairs.english: and he lifted up his eyes and he saw, and, behold, camels coming.
And Rivkah lifted her eyes,
and she saw Isaac [in his grandness],
and she slid from the camel.
And she said to the bondsman:
Who is this man walking in the field towards us?
And the bondsman said: He is my master.
And she took the veil and covered herself.
And the bondsman told Isaac
all the things that he had done [i.e., all the miracles that had been wrought for him.]
And Isaac brought her into the tent, [and she was in stead of] Sarah, his mother [(various miraculous phenomena which had ceased there with Sarah's death, recurring now)].
And she became his wife, and he loved her.
And Isaac was consoled after his mother.
And Abraham married again, a woman
[Hagar], who was called Keturah.
And she bore unto him

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־זִמְרָן֙ וְאֶת־יׇקְשָׁ֔ן וְאֶת־מְדָ֖ן וְאֶת־מִדְיָ֑ן וְאֶת־יִשְׁבָּ֖ק וְאֶת־שֽׁוּחַ׃
pairs.english: Zimran and Yakshan and Medan and Midyan and Yishbak and Shuach.
And Yakshan begot Sheva and Dedan.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י דְדָ֔ן הָי֛וּ אַשּׁוּרִ֥ם וּלְטוּשִׁ֖ם וּלְאֻמִּֽים׃
pairs.english: And the sons of Dedan were [the heads of the peoples:] Ashurim, Letushim, and Leumim.
And the sons of Midyan:
Eifah and Efer and Chanoch and Avida and Elda'ah —
all these the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham gave
all that he had [i.e., the legacy of blessing] to Isaac.
And to the sons of the concubine [Hagar] which Abraham had,
Abraham gave gifts.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֞ם מֵעַ֨ל יִצְחָ֤ק בְּנוֹ֙ בְּעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חַ֔י
pairs.english: And he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he was still alive,
eastward, to the land of the east.
And these are the years of Abraham's life, which he lived:

pairs.hebrew: מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
pairs.english: a hundred years and seventy years, and five years. [A hundred like seventy, and seventy like five — without sin.]
And Abraham expired, and he died in a good old age,
old and content; and he was gathered to his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him [(Ishmael, having repented, granting precedence to Isaac)]

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֞ה עֶפְרֹ֤ן בֶּן־צֹ֙חַר֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃
pairs.english: in the doubled cave in the field of Efron the son of Tzochar, which is before Mamre.
The field which Abraham bought from the sons of Cheth.
There was Abraham buried, and Sarah, his wife.
And it was, after the death of Abraham,
that G d blessed Isaac his son [(the mourners' consolation)].
And Isaac dwelt at Be'er Lachai Ro'i.
And these are the progeny of Ishmael, the son of Abraham,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֜ה הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרָ֖ה לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: whom Hagar the Egyptian, the bondswoman of Sarah, bore to Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל בִּשְׁמֹתָ֖ם לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael by their names in order of birth:

pairs.hebrew: בְּכֹ֤ר יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ נְבָיֹ֔ת וְקֵדָ֥ר וְאַדְבְּאֵ֖ל וּמִבְשָֽׂם׃
pairs.english: the first-born of Ishmael — Nevayoth — and Kedar, and Adbel, and Mivsam.
And Mishma
and Suma
and Massa.
Chadad and Tema,
Yetur, Nafish, and Kedmah.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמֹתָ֔ם בְּחַצְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְטִֽירֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their courts [unwalled cities] and by their strongholds —
twelve princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of the life of Ishmael:

pairs.hebrew: מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים
pairs.english: a hundred years, and thirty years, and seven years.
And he expired [in righteousness] and he died, and he was gathered to his people.
And they dwelt from Chavilah until Shur,
which is before Egypt on the way to Ashur.
In the presence of all his brethren he dwelt.
And these [(Jacob and Esau)] are the progeny of Isaac the son of Abraham.
Abraham begot Isaac [i.e., After he was called "Abraham," he begot Isaac].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י יִצְחָק֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֶת־רִבְקָ֗ה בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י
pairs.english: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rivkah the daughter of Bethuel the Aramite [(an evildoer)]
from Padan Aram [(a place of evildoers)],
the sister of Lavan the Aramite [(an evildoer)]
to himself as a wife, [(Rivkah retaining her integrity in spite of the above associations)].
And Isaac entreated the L rd, [praying] opposite his wife,
for she was barren.
And the L rd was entreated of him, [(but not of her, the prayer of a righteous child of a wicked father not being comparable to that of a righteous child of a righteous father)],
and Rivkah his wife conceived.
And the children wrangled within her,
and she said: If so [great is the pain of pregnancy], why (did) I [so much desire and pray for] this?
And she went [to the school of Shem] to inquire of the L rd [as to what was portended for her.]
And the L rd said to her [through Shem]: Two nations are in your womb,
and two kingdoms from your innards shall part, [one to do evil, the other to do good],
and one kingdom shall gain strength from the other, [i.e., As one falls, the other shall rise],
and the elder shall serve the younger.
And her days were filled to give birth,
and, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And the first one came out ruddy,
all like a hairy cloak,
and they called his name Esau ["all made" (i.e., complete)].

pairs.hebrew: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן יָצָ֣א אָחִ֗יו וְיָד֤וֹ אֹחֶ֙זֶת֙ בַּעֲקֵ֣ב עֵשָׂ֔ו
pairs.english: And after his brother went out, his hand grasping Esau's heel (akev), [(portending his seizure of Esau's kingdom before its consummation)],
and he called his name Yaakov.
And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
And when the youths grew up,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ צַ֖יִד אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: Esau became a man versed in deception, a man of the field [i.e., a hunter],
and Jacob a whole (-hearted) man, a dweller of tents [i.e., of (the schools of) Shem and Ever].
And Isaac loved Esau, for [Esau "placed"] venison in his mouth,
and Rivkah loved Jacob.
And Jacob cooked a pottage,
and Esau came from the field and he was faint [with murder.]
And Esau said to Jacob:

pairs.hebrew: הַלְעִיטֵ֤נִי נָא֙ מִן־הָאָדֹ֤ם הָאָדֹם֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י עָיֵ֖ף אָנֹ֑כִי
pairs.english: "Pour down (my throat) some of this red (adom) red stuff, for I am faint"
— wherefore his name was called Edom.
And Jacob said:
Sell [as "clearly"] as the day [is clear] your birthright to me. [An evildoer such as you is not worthy of the sacrificial service (which is the prerogative of the first-born.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י הוֹלֵ֖ךְ לָמ֑וּת
pairs.english: And Esau said: Behold, I am going to die.
What need have I, then, of this birthright?
And Jacob said: Swear to me as the day [is clear].
And he swore to him,
and he sold his birthright to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וְיַעֲקֹ֞ב נָתַ֣ן לְעֵשָׂ֗ו לֶ֚חֶם וּנְזִ֣יד עֲדָשִׁ֔ים
pairs.english: And Jacob gave to Esau bread and a pottage of lentils.
And he ate, and he drank, and he arose, and he went, and
[(Scripture testifying to this effect)] Esau shamed the birthright.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: And there was a famine in the land, aside from the first famine in the days of Abraham.
And Isaac went to Avimelech, king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה
pairs.english: And the L rd appeared to him and said: Do not go down to Egypt, [for you are a "pure burnt-offering"];
dwell in the land that I shall indicate to you.

pairs.hebrew: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ
pairs.english: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and I will bless you.
For to you and to your seed will I give all of these lands.

pairs.hebrew: וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת־הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: And I will fulfill the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
And I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens,
and I will give to your seed all of these lands,
and there will bless themselves in [the name of] your seed all the nations of the land.
Because Abraham heeded My voice [when I tried him],

and he kept My keeping [i.e., decrees for the safekeeping of the exhortations of the Torah], My mitzvoth [self-evident moral imperatives], My statutes [decrees inaccessible to reason], and My laws [(including the oral law)].
And Isaac dwelt
in Gerar.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said: "She is my sister."

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן־יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל־רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי־טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽוא׃
pairs.english: For he feared to say: "She is my wife," lest the men of the place kill me because of Rivkah, for she is very fair.
And it was, when the days were grown long for him there, [Isaac thinking that Rivkah was no longer in danger and relaxing his vigil],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן
pairs.english: that Avimelech the king of the Philistines looked through the window,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and behold, Isaac sporting [i.e., lying] with Rivkah his wife.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And Avimelech called to Isaac and he said: But she is surely your wife! How, then, did you tell me: "She is my sister"?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: And Isaac said to him: For I said: Lest I die because of her.
And Avimelech said: What is this that you have done to us?
The [distinctive] one of the people [i.e., the king] had almost lain with your wife,
and, [had he done so], you would have brought guilt upon us.
And Avimelech commanded all the people, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
pairs.english: Whoever touches this man or his wife shall be put to death.
And Isaac sowed in that land [(though it was not so fertile as the land of the seven nations)],
and he found in that year, [a difficult year], a hundredfold [more than the estimated yield].
And the L rd blessed him.
And the man grew (i.e., prospered),

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי־גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃
pairs.english: and he continued growing, until he had grown exceedingly.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה־צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And he had flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and much labor,
and the Philistines envied him.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And all of the wells that the servants of his father had dug in the days of Abraham, his father,
were stopped up by the Philistines [(as abetting invading armies)], and they filled them up with sand.
And Avimelech said to Isaac:
Go away from us, for you have grown much stronger than we.
And Isaac went thence,
and he camped in the valley of Gerar, and he dwelt there.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨שׇׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר ׀ אֶת־בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו
pairs.english: And Isaac returned [(before he left Gerar)] and dug the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father
and which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃
pairs.english: And he called them by the names by which his father had called them.
And the servants of Isaac dug in the valley,
and they found there a well of living waters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with the shepherds of Isaac, saying: "The water is ours!"

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם־הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And he called the name of the well Esek ("contention"), for they contended with him [over it].
And they dug another well,
and they quarreled over it, too,
and they called its name Sitnah ("constraint").

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: And he traveled from there, and he dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it;

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהֹוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and he called its name Rechovoth ("widening"), saying: For now the L rd has "widened" (things) for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.
And he went up from there
to Beersheva.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהֹוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And the L rd appeared to him that night, and He said: I am the G d of Abraham your father.

pairs.hebrew: אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֙יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי׃
pairs.english: Do not fear, for I am with you. And I shall bless you and I shall multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham, My servant.
And he built an altar there,
and he called in the name of the L rd.
And he pitched his tent there,
and the servants of Isaac dug a well there.
And Avimelech went to him from Gerar
and a company of his friends and Phichol the captain of his host.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to them: Why have you come to me
when you hate me and you sent me away from you?
And they said: We saw [in you as] we saw [in your father] that the L rd was with you.

pairs.hebrew: וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And we said: Let the oath that was between us [from the days of your father, also] be between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק־ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם
pairs.english: That you do not evil to us just as we did not touch you and just as we did with you only good and we sent you away in peace.
You [too, do] now [likewise unto us], O blessed of the L rd.
And he made a feast for them,
and they ate and drank.
And they arose early in the morning, and they swore to each other,
and Isaac sent them away, and they went from him in peace.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק
pairs.english: And it was on that day that the servants of Isaac came

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ
pairs.english: and told him about the well they had dug;
and they said to him: We have found water.
And he called it Shivah ("covenanting").
Therefore, the name of the city is Beersheva ("the well of the covenant")
until this day.
And when Esau was forty years,
he took as a wife Yehudith, the daughter of Be'eri the Hittite,
and Basmath, the daughter of Eilon the Hittite.
And they were a vexation of spirit
to Isaac and to Rivkah [in that they served idolatry].
And it was, when Isaac became old,
that his eyes grew dulled from seeing.
And he called to Esau, his elder son,
saying to him: "My son."
And he said to him: "Here I am."
And he said: Behold, I have become old;
I do not know the day of my death.
And now, take [(also connoting "sharpen")] I pray you, your knives [for shechitah (ritual slaughter)], your sword and your bow,
and go out into the field, and hunt me a hunting, [and not theft].

pairs.hebrew: וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֨י מַטְעַמִּ֜ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהַ֛בְתִּי וְהָבִ֥יאָה לִּ֖י וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
pairs.english: And make me the kind of tasty dish that I like, and bring it to me and I shall eat it,
so that my soul bless you before I die.

pairs.hebrew: וְרִבְקָ֣ה שֹׁמַ֔עַת בְּדַבֵּ֣ר יִצְחָ֔ק אֶל־עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Rivkah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ עֵשָׂו֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָצ֥וּד צַ֖יִד לְהָבִֽיא׃
pairs.english: and Esau went to the field to hunt a hunting to bring [by theft, if "hunting" were not available].
And Rivkah said to Jacob her son:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־אָבִ֔יךָ מְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶל־עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יךָ לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: Behold, I have overheard your father saying to your brother Esau:

pairs.hebrew: הָבִ֨יאָה לִּ֥י צַ֛יִד וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֥י מַטְעַמִּ֖ים וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
pairs.english: Bring me a hunting and make me savory food, and I shall eat,
and I shall bless you before the L rd [i.e., by His leave] before my death.
And now, my son, hearken to my voice,
to what I command you.

pairs.hebrew: לֶךְ־נָא֙ אֶל־הַצֹּ֔אן וְקַֽח־לִ֣י מִשָּׁ֗ם שְׁנֵ֛י גְּדָיֵ֥י עִזִּ֖ים טֹבִ֑ים
pairs.english: Go, now, to the flock, and take for me [(from what is mine)] from there two good goat kids, [one for a paschal offering, and one for a savory dish],

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֨ה אֹתָ֧ם מַטְעַמִּ֛ים לְאָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהֵֽב׃
pairs.english: and I shall make of them for your father the kind of tasty dish that he likes [(kid, tasting like venison)].
And bring it to your father and have him eat,
so that he bless you before his death.
And Jacob said to Rivkah, his mother:

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֣ן עֵשָׂ֤ו אָחִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂעִ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִ֥ישׁ חָלָֽק׃
pairs.english: But Esau my brother is hairy and I am smooth-skinned.
Perchance my father will feel me
and I shall be in his eyes as a deceiver,
and I will bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing!

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִמּ֔וֹ עָלַ֥י קִלְלָתְךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And his mother said to him: Your curse upon me, my son;
only hear my voice and go take (them) for me.
And he went and took (them) and brought (them) to his mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַתַּ֤עַשׂ אִמּוֹ֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָהֵ֥ב אָבִֽיו׃
pairs.english: And his mother made the kind of tasty dish that his father liked.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִ֠בְקָ֠ה אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֨י עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּנָ֤הּ הַגָּדֹל֙ הַחֲמֻדֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּ֖הּ בַּבָּ֑יִת
pairs.english: And Rivkah took the clean garments of Esau, her elder son, which were with her [for safe-keeping] in the house,
and she clothed Jacob her younger son with them.
And the skins of the goat-kids
she placed upon his hands and the smooth of his neck.
And she placed the tasty dish and the bread that she had made
in the hand of her son Jacob.
And he brought (it) to his father, and he said: "My father."
And he said: "I am here. Who are you, my son?"

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־אָבִ֗יו אָנֹכִי֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּכֹרֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And Jacob said to his father: I am [(the one bringing food to you, and)] Esau [is] your first-born.
I have done [(many things)] as you have spoken to me.

pairs.hebrew: קֽוּם־נָ֣א שְׁבָ֗ה וְאׇכְלָה֙ מִצֵּידִ֔י בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרְכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
pairs.english: Arise, I pray you, and sit [at table] and eat of my hunting so that your soul bless me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶל־בְּנ֔וֹ מַה־זֶּ֛ה מִהַ֥רְתָּ לִמְצֹ֖א בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to his son: How did you find (it) so quickly, my son?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י הִקְרָ֛ה יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנָֽי׃
pairs.english: And he said: For the L rd your G d put it in my way.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב גְּשָׁה־נָּ֥א וַאֲמֻֽשְׁךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to Jacob: Come near and let me feel you, my son, [(Isaac having been surprised at the reply, atypical of Esau)].
Are you my son Esau or not?
And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father, and he felt him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקֹּל֙ ק֣וֹל יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְהַיָּדַ֖יִם יְדֵ֥י עֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: and he said: The voice [i.e., the tone, e.g., "Arise, I pray you"] is the voice of Jacob [(as opposed to Esau's brusque "Let my father arise")], but the hands are the hands of Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֣א הִכִּיר֔וֹ כִּֽי־הָי֣וּ יָדָ֗יו כִּידֵ֛י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יו שְׂעִרֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And he did not recognize him, for his hands were like the hands of Esau his brother, hairy,
and he blessed him.
And he said: Are you this, my son Esau?
And he said: "I" [(but not: "I am Esau.")]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַגִּ֤שָׁה לִּי֙ וְאֹֽכְלָה֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנִ֔י לְמַ֥עַן תְּבָֽרֶכְךָ֖ נַפְשִׁ֑י
pairs.english: And he said: Reach (it) to me, and I will eat of the hunting of my son, so that my soul bless you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגֶּשׁ־לוֹ֙ וַיֹּאכַ֔ל וַיָּ֧בֵא ל֦וֹ יַ֖יִן וַיֵּֽשְׁתְּ׃
pairs.english: And he reached (it) to him, and he ate, and he brought him wine and he drank.
And Isaac his father said to him:
Draw near, now, and kiss me, my son.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ וַיִּשַּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֛רַח אֶת־רֵ֥יחַ בְּגָדָ֖יו וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: And he drew near and he kissed him and he smelled the smell of his garments [into which the fragrance of Eden had entered], and he blessed him.
And he said: See, the smell of my son
is as that of a field [of apples] which the L rd has blessed.
And may G d give you [in addition to the fragrance of Eden]

pairs.hebrew: מִטַּל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹ֥ב דָּגָ֖ן וְתִירֹֽשׁ׃
pairs.english: of the dew of the heavens and the fat of the earth, and an abundance of corn and wine.
Peoples will serve you, and nations will bow down to you.

pairs.hebrew: הֱוֵ֤ה גְבִיר֙ לְאַחֶ֔יךָ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: Be a master to your brothers, and your mother's sons will bow down to you.
Your cursers will be cursed and your blessers will be blessed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלָּ֣ה יִצְחָק֮ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒
pairs.english: And it was, when Isaac finished blessing Jacob —

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י אַ֣ךְ יָצֹ֤א יָצָא֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב מֵאֵ֥ת פְּנֵ֖י יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: Jacob had just left the presence of Isaac his father,
when Esau his brother came from his hunting.
And he, too, made a savory dish and brought it to his father.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֗יו יָקֻ֤ם אָבִי֙ וְיֹאכַל֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנ֔וֹ בַּעֲבֻ֖ר תְּבָרְכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
pairs.english: And he said to his father: Let my father arise and eat from the hunting of his son, so that your soul bless me.
And Isaac his father said to him: Who are you?
And he said: I am your first-born son, Esau.
And Isaac was greatly confounded,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר מִֽי־אֵפ֡וֹא ה֣וּא הַצָּֽד־צַ֩יִד֩ וַיָּ֨בֵא לִ֜י וָאֹכַ֥ל מִכֹּ֛ל בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא וָאֲבָרְכֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: and he said: Who is it, then, that hunted a hunting and brought it to me and I ate all [the flavors that I desired] before you came, and I blessed him —
and he will, indeed, be blessed.
When Esau heard the words of his father,
he cried a great and bitter outcry,
and he said to his father: Bless me also, my father!
And he said:
Your brother came with subtlety and took your blessing.
And he said: "Is it for this that he was called 'Yaakov' ('following at the heels')?
That he would overtake me (ya'akveini) these two times?
He took my birthright,
and, behold, now he has taken my blessing!"
And he said: "Did you not keep back a blessing for me?"

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨עַן יִצְחָ֜ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵשָׂ֗ו הֵ֣ן גְּבִ֞יר שַׂמְתִּ֥יו לָךְ֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־אֶחָ֗יו נָתַ֤תִּי לוֹ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים
pairs.english: And Isaac answered and he said to Esau: I made him a master over you, and all of his brothers have I given to him as bondsmen [and "whatever a bondsman acquires is acquired by his master"],
and with corn and wine have I buttressed him,
and for you, then, what can I do, my son?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶל־אָבִ֗יו הַֽבְרָכָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת הִֽוא־לְךָ֙ אָבִ֔י
pairs.english: And Esau said to his father: Do you have only one blessing, my father?
Bless me, too, my father.
And Esau raised his voice and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and he said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֞ה מִשְׁמַנֵּ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ וּמִטַּ֥ל הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מֵעָֽל׃
pairs.english: Behold, of the fats of the earth [Graeca Magna] will be your dwelling, and of the dew of the heavens from above.
And by your sword will you live, and your brother will you serve.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֔יד וּפָרַקְתָּ֥ עֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֥ל צַוָּארֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: And it shall be when you [have just reason to] grieve [over the blessings' having been appropriated by Jacob (i.e., when Israel transgresses the Torah)], then you shall remove his yoke from your neck.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂטֹ֤ם עֵשָׂו֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב עַ֨ל־הַבְּרָכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּרְכ֖וֹ אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing that his father had given him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּלִבּ֗וֹ יִקְרְבוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ אֵ֣בֶל אָבִ֔י וְאַֽהַרְגָ֖ה אֶת־יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽי׃
pairs.english: and Esau said in his heart; Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, and I will [then] kill Jacob my brother [(and not before, so as not to aggrieve my father)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְרִבְקָ֔ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנָ֣הּ הַגָּדֹ֑ל
pairs.english: And it was told to Rivkah [through the holy spirit] the thoughts of Esau her elder son,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּשְׁלַ֞ח וַתִּקְרָ֤א לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּנָ֣הּ הַקָּטָ֔ן וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו
pairs.english: and she sent and called to Jacob her younger son and said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֔יךָ מִתְנַחֵ֥ם לְךָ֖ לְהׇרְגֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: Behold, Esau your brother is bethinking himself [of his brotherhood] to you, to kill you.
And now, my son, hearken to my voice.
Arise, and run away to Lavan my brother in Charan.
And remain with him for some time,
until your brother's fury is abated.

pairs.hebrew: עַד־שׁ֨וּב אַף־אָחִ֜יךָ מִמְּךָ֗ וְשָׁכַח֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: Until your brother's wrath turns from you and he forgets what you did to him,
when I will send and take you from there.
Why should I be bereft of both of you [(one killing, the other being killed in revenge)] in one day [(a presage of the future, Jacob and Esau being buried on the same day)] (See Sotah 13a).

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רִבְקָה֙ אֶל־יִצְחָ֔ק קַ֣צְתִּי בְחַיַּ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנ֣וֹת חֵ֑ת
pairs.english: And Rivkah said to Isaac: I have despised my life because of the daughters of Cheth.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־לֹקֵ֣חַ יַ֠עֲקֹ֠ב אִשָּׁ֨ה מִבְּנֽוֹת־חֵ֤ת כָּאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִבְּנ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לָ֥מָּה לִּ֖י חַיִּֽים׃
pairs.english: If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Cheth such as these of the daughters of the land, what is life to me?
And Isaac called to Jacob and he blessed him,
and he charged him, saying:
Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: Arise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father,

pairs.hebrew: וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃
pairs.english: and take for yourself from there a wife from the daughters of Lavan, your mother's brother.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And the G d who is All-Sufficient [in His blessings] will bless you. And He will make you fruitful and will multiply you,
and you will be an assembly of peoples.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ אֶת־בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: And He will give you [i.e., there will issue from you] the blessing of [i.e., to] Abraham [(12:2): "And I shall make you a great nation" and (26:4): "And they will bless themselves in your seed"], to you and to your seed with you,

pairs.hebrew: לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: to inherit the land of your sojournings which G d gave to Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Isaac sent Jacob, and he went to Padan-Aram,

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־לָבָ֤ן בֶּן־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: to Lavan the son of Bethuel the Aramite, the brother of Rivkah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי־בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת־ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and that he had sent him to Padan-Aram to take for himself from there a wife

pairs.hebrew: בְּבָרְכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃
pairs.english: in blessing him, charging him: Do not take wife from the daughters of Canaan,
and that Jacob had heeded his father and mother
and gone to Padan-Aram.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were evil
in the eyes of Isaac his father.
And Esau [likewise] went to Ishmael,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת ׀ בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת
pairs.english: and he took Machlath the daughter of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, the sister of Nevayoth [(who gave her in marriage to Esau)]
in addition to his (other) [wicked] wives for himself as a wife.
